caption:
"My wife skipped our son’s emergency surgery for a ‘mental health retreat’ that turned out to be a first-class getaway with her tennis instructor. She didn’t know I was watching the transaction alerts roll in while holding our boy’s hand in the ICU. I waited until she was at the front of the TSA PreCheck line—surrounded by people—before I nuked the flights, froze the joint accounts, and sent her a single photo that ended her life as she knew it. The meltdown she had at Terminal 4 wasn’t just embarrassing; it was a masterpiece of instant karma.

CHAPTER 1

The sound of a pediatric ICU isn’t loud. It’s the silence that kills you.

It’s a heavy, suffocating silence punctuated only by the rhythmic whoosh-click of a ventilator and the steady, hypnotic beep of a heart monitor.

I was sitting in a plastic chair that was designed to be uncomfortable, presumably so parents wouldn’t fall asleep while their world fell apart. My hand was wrapped around Leo’s.

Leo is five. His hand was so small in mine, his knuckles pale, an IV line taped to the back of his wrist with a picture of a cartoon dog on the bandage.

Viral pneumonia. Complicated by asthma. That’s what the doctors said. To me, it just looked like my son was drowning in plain sight, and I couldn't swim fast enough to save him.

I hadn’t slept in thirty-six hours. My eyes felt like they were filled with sand. My shirt, a wrinkled blue Oxford from the office, smelled like stale coffee and fear.

I checked my watch. 8:15 PM.

Elena should have been here four hours ago.

""She’s just overwhelmed, Mark,"" she had told me on the phone that morning, her voice trembling with that fragile, victimized tone she had perfected over seven years of marriage. ""Seeing him like that... with the tubes... it triggers my anxiety. I need to step away. Just for a few hours. To decompress. For Leo's sake.""

I had bought it. I always bought it. I was the provider, the rock, the stoic husband who absorbed the shockwaves so she could remain delicate and untouched.

""Go,"" I had said, hating myself for it even as the words left my mouth. ""Go to your mom’s. Get some rest. I’ll handle the doctors.""

She had kissed me on the cheek—a dry, glancing peck—and walked out. She didn't look back at Leo. She didn't look back at me. She just grabbed her Louis Vuitton tote, the one I bought her for our anniversary, and clicked her heels down the hospital corridor.

That was ten hours ago.

I picked up my phone to text her again. The screen was full of my one-sided desperation.

He’s waking up soon. Please come back.
Doctor wants to discuss the lung scan.
Elena? Are you at your mom’s?

Nothing. No read receipts. Just the grey void of delivered messages.

Then, the phone buzzed. Not a text. A notification from the Amex app.

I frowned. I rubbed my eyes, thinking I was hallucinating from exhaustion. I unlocked the phone and stared at the banner across the top of the screen.

Card Not Present Transaction Approved: $4,850.00 - DELTA AIRLINES.

I blinked.

Maybe it was a mistake. Fraud. Someone stole the card numbers. That had to be it. Elena was at her mother's house in Jersey, probably crying on the sofa with a glass of Pinot Grigio, too distraught to answer her phone.

Then the second buzz came.

Card Not Present Transaction Approved: $2,100.00 - THE RESORT AT PEDREGAL - CABO SAN LUCAS.

My stomach dropped. It wasn't a slow sinking feeling; it was a freefall. The air in the room suddenly felt too thin.

I looked at Leo. He was sleeping, his chest rising and falling in shallow, labored breaths. My son was fighting for every ounce of oxygen, and my credit card was currently booking a five-star vacation in Mexico.

My hands started to shake. Not from fear, but from a cold, sharp rage that started at the base of my spine.

I opened the banking app. I didn't call her. I didn't text her asking ""What is this?""

I’m a forensic accountant. I don’t react to data; I analyze it. I follow the trail.

I logged into our shared cloud account. Elena wasn't tech-savvy. She thought deleting a text message meant it was gone forever. She didn't understand that everything backs up if you don't toggle the right switches.

I sat there, in the dim blue light of the ICU monitor, and I scrolled.

I found the folder. ""Synced Photos.""

There was a selfie taken two hours ago.

It wasn't Elena crying on her mother's couch.

It was Elena in the backseat of an Uber, wearing those oversized Dior sunglasses and a white sundress I’d never seen before. She was smiling. Not a nervous, anxious smile. A predatory, excited smile.

And she wasn't alone.

Leaning into the frame, kissing her cheek, was a guy. I recognized him instantly.

Julian.

The ""tennis coach."" The guy she swore was ""just a kid"" trying to pay his way through grad school. The guy I had tipped fifty bucks last Christmas because Elena said he was ""struggling.""

I scrolled to the next photo. It was a picture of two passports on a table at a bar. A caption was typed over it in a curly, cute font: Finally escaping the gloom. Don’t wait up, hubby. 😉

She hadn’t posted it to Instagram. She had sent it to a group chat named ""Manifesting Queens.""

I clicked on the messages.

Elena: I feel a little bad leaving Leo, but Mark is so intense about it. He suffocates the room. I just need to breathe. Besides, Julian promised me tequila and sunsets.

Friend 1: You deserve it, babe! Caregiver burnout is real!

Elena: Exactly. Plus, Mark won’t notice. He’s too busy playing the martyr at the hospital. I’ll tell him I had a breakdown and turned my phone off. He’ll apologize to ME for worrying.

I read that last line three times.

He’ll apologize to ME.

She knew me. She knew exactly how to manipulate my protective instincts. She knew I would shoulder the burden, make excuses for her, and apologize for not making her life perfect enough.

She was banking on my love for her. She was banking on my distraction with our dying son.

I looked up from the phone. The nurse, a kind woman named Sarah, walked in to check Leo’s vitals.

""How are you holding up, Dad?"" she whispered, adjusting the drip.

""I'm managing,"" I said. My voice sounded strange. calm. Robotic. ""Sarah, is the Wi-Fi in here secure? I have some work to do.""

""It's pretty good,"" she smiled sympathetically. ""Work doesn't stop, huh?""

""No,"" I said, my eyes drifting back to the picture of Julian’s hand on my wife’s thigh. ""It doesn't.""

I waited until Sarah left.

I looked at the time. 8:30 PM.

The flight to Cabo departed from JFK at 10:45 PM. That meant they were likely checking in right now, or going through security. They were probably laughing about how easy it was. Using my points. Using my money. Using my trust.

I could call her. I could scream. I could demand she come back.

But that’s what the old Mark would do. The Mark who wanted to save the marriage.

That Mark died the second I saw the charge for the resort.

The man sitting in the chair now was different. This man was a calculator. This man was a demolition expert.

I opened the Delta app. Since the tickets were bought on my card, linked to my SkyMiles account, they were right there on the dashboard.

Passenger: Elena Vance.
Passenger: Julian Rivas.
Seat: 1A, 1B. First Class.

She didn't even have the decency to fly coach with my money.

I stared at the ""Modify Flight"" button.

Too easy.

If I cancelled it now, she’d just get a notification. She might be able to talk her way onto another flight, or use her own emergency card.

No.

I needed this to hurt. I needed this to be public. I needed her to be stranded, humiliated, and cut off, exactly when she felt the safest.

I needed to time this perfectly.

I pulled up the airport map on my laptop. I checked the TSA wait times at JFK Terminal 4. They were heavy. 45 minutes.

If they were checking bags—and Elena always checked bags, usually three of them—they would be at the counter right about... now.

I logged into the Amex portal.

I didn't just want to stop the transaction. I wanted to flag it.

I navigated to the ""Dispute Charge"" section.

Reason for dispute?

I typed two words: Unauthorized/Theft.

Then I called the number on the back of the card. I have a Platinum card, which means a human answers immediately.

""American Express, this is Jennifer. How can I help you, Mr. Vance?""

""Hi Jennifer,"" I said, my voice steady, my eyes fixed on my son’s sleeping face. ""I need to report a stolen card. And I need you to understand the urgency. The thief is currently attempting to use it at JFK airport.""

""Oh my goodness,"" Jennifer said. ""I can freeze the account immediately. Do you want me to cancel the pending charges for Delta and the resort?""

""Yes,"" I said. ""Cancel them. Hard decline. And Jennifer?""

""Yes, sir?""

""Mark the card as lost and stolen. Notify the merchants that the user is fraudulent. I want the system to flash red when they try to swipe it again.""

""Done,"" she said. ""The account is frozen. The tickets are being voided as we speak. Is there anything else?""

""No,"" I said. ""That should be enough for now.""

I hung up.

I watched the clock. 8:38 PM.

They would be at the front of the line. The agent would be asking for passports. Elena would be smiling, flipping her hair, waiting for her boarding pass to the good life.

I imagined the agent swiping the card for the baggage fees. Or better yet, pulling up the reservation and seeing the big, flashing VOID status.

My phone buzzed again.

It wasn't a transaction this time.

It was a text from Elena.

Elena: Baby, I’m at my mom’s. I took a Xanax and I’m going to try to sleep. My phone is dying so I might not reply for a bit. Kiss Leo for me. Love you.

I stared at the lie. It was so casual. So practiced.

I didn't reply.

Instead, I opened my laptop and went to the home security system. I deactivated her code.

Then I logged into our Tesla account. The car she had taken to the airport. I saw the location: JFK Terminal 4 Parking, Level 2.

I enabled ""Valet Mode."" Then I enabled ""Pin to Drive.""

She wasn't just losing her flight. She was losing her ride home.

But I wasn't done.

I looked at Leo again. He stirred, his eyes fluttering open.

""Daddy?"" he rasped.

My heart broke and hardened at the same time. I leaned in, smoothing his hair.

""I'm here, buddy. I'm right here.""

""Where's Mommy?"" he whispered.

The rage flared up, hot and white, threatening to burn through my skin. But I kept my voice soft.

""Mommy had to go, Leo. But don't worry. I'm going to take care of everything.""

I kissed his forehead and waited for him to drift back to sleep.

Once he was out, I stood up. I walked to the window of the hospital room, looking out at the city lights. Somewhere out there, near the horizon, my wife was about to have the worst night of her life.

And the best part? She thought she was the one holding all the cards.

I cracked my knuckles.

It was time to pack her bags.

I looked up from the phone. The nurse, a kind woman named Sarah, walked in to check Leo’s vitals.

""How are you holding up, Dad?"" she whispered, adjusting the drip.

""I'm managing,"" I said. My voice sounded strange. calm. Robotic. ""Sarah, is the Wi-Fi in here secure? I have some work to do.""

""It's pretty good,"" she smiled sympathetically. ""Work doesn't stop, huh?""

""No,"" I said, my eyes drifting back to the picture of Julian’s hand on my wife’s thigh. ""It doesn't.""

I waited until Sarah left.

I looked at the time. 8:30 PM.

The flight to Cabo departed from JFK at 10:45 PM. That meant they were likely checking in right now, or going through security. They were probably laughing about how easy it was. Using my points. Using my money. Using my trust.

I could call her. I could scream. I could demand she come back.

But that’s what the old Mark would do. The Mark who wanted to save the marriage.

That Mark died the second I saw the charge for the resort.

The man sitting in the chair now was different. This man was a calculator. This man was a demolition expert.

I opened the Delta app. Since the tickets were bought on my card, linked to my SkyMiles account, they were right there on the dashboard.

Passenger: Elena Vance.
Passenger: Julian Rivas.
Seat: 1A, 1B. First Class.

She didn't even have the decency to fly coach with my money.

I stared at the ""Modify Flight"" button.

Too easy.

If I cancelled it now, she’d just get a notification. She might be able to talk her way onto another flight, or use her own emergency card.

No.

I needed this to hurt. I needed this to be public. I needed her to be stranded, humiliated, and cut off, exactly when she felt the safest.

I needed to time this perfectly.

I pulled up the airport map on my laptop. I checked the TSA wait times at JFK Terminal 4. They were heavy. 45 minutes.

If they were checking bags—and Elena always checked bags, usually three of them—they would be at the counter right about... now.

I logged into the Amex portal.

I didn't just want to stop the transaction. I wanted to flag it.

I navigated to the ""Dispute Charge"" section.

Reason for dispute?

I typed two words: Unauthorized/Theft.

Then I called the number on the back of the card. I have a Platinum card, which means a human answers immediately.

""American Express, this is Jennifer. How can I help you, Mr. Vance?""

""Hi Jennifer,"" I said, my voice steady, my eyes fixed on my son’s sleeping face. ""I need to report a stolen card. And I need you to understand the urgency. The thief is currently attempting to use it at JFK airport.""

""Oh my goodness,"" Jennifer said. ""I can freeze the account immediately. Do you want me to cancel the pending charges for Delta and the resort?""

""Yes,"" I said. ""Cancel them. Hard decline. And Jennifer?""

""Yes, sir?""

""Mark the card as lost and stolen. Notify the merchants that the user is fraudulent. I want the system to flash red when they try to swipe it again.""

""Done,"" she said. ""The account is frozen. The tickets are being voided as we speak. Is there anything else?""

""No,"" I said. ""That should be enough for now.""

I hung up.

I watched the clock. 8:38 PM.

They would be at the front of the line. The agent would be asking for passports. Elena would be smiling, flipping her hair, waiting for her boarding pass to the good life.

I imagined the agent swiping the card for the baggage fees. Or better yet, pulling up the reservation and seeing the big, flashing VOID status.

My phone buzzed again.

It wasn't a transaction this time.

It was a text from Elena.

Elena: Baby, I’m at my mom’s. I took a Xanax and I’m going to try to sleep. My phone is dying so I might not reply for a bit. Kiss Leo for me. Love you.

I stared at the lie. It was so casual. So practiced.

I didn't reply.

Instead, I opened my laptop and went to the home security system. I deactivated her code.

Then I logged into our Tesla account. The car she had taken to the airport. I saw the location: JFK Terminal 4 Parking, Level 2.

I enabled ""Valet Mode."" Then I enabled ""Pin to Drive.""

She wasn't just losing her flight. She was losing her ride home.

But I wasn't done.

I looked at Leo again. He stirred, his eyes fluttering open.

""Daddy?"" he rasped.

My heart broke and hardened at the same time. I leaned in, smoothing his hair.

""I'm here, buddy. I'm right here.""

""Where's Mommy?"" he whispered.

The rage flared up, hot and white, threatening to burn through my skin. But I kept my voice soft.

""Mommy had to go, Leo. But don't worry. I'm going to take care of everything.""

I kissed his forehead and waited for him to drift back to sleep.

Once he was out, I stood up. I walked to the window of the hospital room, looking out at the city lights. Somewhere out there, near the horizon, my wife was about to have the worst night of her life.

And the best part? She thought she was the one holding all the cards.

I cracked my knuckles.

It was time to pack her bags.

caption:
As we celebrate #10YearsOfJanDhan, it is remarkable to  think of the complex mapping and the step-by-step stacking of the economic architecture that PM Modi had in his mind from the beginning itself. 

Remember, Jan Dhan is the FIRST flagship scheme of PM Modi, launched within months of his tenure. It, thus, came from his own deeply held beliefs rather than any 'expert' advice. 

First task was to set the base 

Jan Dhan (in 2014), giving legal architecture to Aadhar (2015-16) and the new telecom policy of 2015 enabled the JAM trinity which fundamentally changed India. 

Because the poorest, who need state enabling hand the most, were now in formal financial systems. 

JAM trinity, built on base of Jan Dhan enabled: 

1) DBT (2014): Ending the poverty parade and indignity of queuing up to get your rightful benefits (0ver 38 lakhs crore transferred so far). 

2) Mudra Loans (2015): Collateral free, affordable loans ending reign of informal sector loan sharks and perpetual loans traps (0ver 46 Cr loans). 

3) Social Security (2015): Life Insurance, accidental insurance and pension schemes - an entire bouquet which had never reached over 50 Cr people was now enabled. (Over 45 CR beneficiaries) 

4) Housing - PM Aawaas (2015): Jan Dhan assured the subsidy reached the indented, targeted, and deserving beneficiary. (Over 4 Cr homes)

4) Crop Insurance: PM Fasal Bima (2016) worked, when all previous failed, because among other reasons the farmers were assured of their insurance payout when needed. (Over 8 Cr farmers covered)

5) UPI - Digital Payments (2016): The unprecedented mass scaling and success happened only because it connected the entire spectrum - from fruit selling village vendor to the  household maid. (40% of world wide digital payments take place India alone).

6) Ayushman Bharat (2018) - The world's largest health scheme, a product which the poor earlier had no hopes of even dreaming about, was now a reality. (over 50 Cr beneficiaries) 

7) Farm Incidental Expense - PM Kisan (2019): Identified and verified marginal farmer was now in the financial system. Reachable directly. (over 11 Cr farmers covered)

8) Crisis support (2020-21): The assured, timely and leak proof support millions of people during COVID-19 induced lockdown. It is an underappreciated achievement - the way in which the government support helped the country tide over the pandemic.

9) Street Vendors - PM SVANidhi (2020): Such is the sophistication of Jan Dhan by now, that banks were confident of giving loans to even street vendors!

But beyond the obvious and headline numbers, the real impact of Jan Dhan has been this: 

_______________

Jan Dhan ended the indignity of the poor. 

The indignity that came at the end of the day to a MNREGA worker who had to shell out a cut from his hard earned money to the middleman. 

The indignity that came to a poor women entrepreneur who went to take a loan but the banks refused and she was caught in the loan shark world.

The indignity of being unable to get hospital treatment for your loved ones and the helplessness that brought. 

So while Jan Dhan solved the basic needs of the poor one one spectrum and enabled a digital revolution at the other, at the basic level it ignited a sense of empowerment and dignity in the poor. Once cannot but overstate the multiplier effects that this has on the destinies of the country. 

In the history of economic reforms since 1991,  Jan Dhan, launched not under coercion but as a commitment, is inarguably the greatest reform with the most positive after-effects. 

Among PM Modi's most enduring legacies, Jan Dhan will remain among the very top - remarkable considering what else has as achieved (Article 370, Ram Mandir to just name two). 

And to think that PM Modi had all this mapped out in advance in 2014 itself !

- Akhilesh Mishra

caption:
Modi Government Is Giving Rs. 10 Lakhs. Apply Today 💸

Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) provides micro-credit to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro-enterprises in India. It supports income-generating activities through various financial institutions.

Key Points:

 * Micro-credit scheme for non-corporate small Indian businesses.

 * Provides loans up to ₹10 lakh for business purposes.

 * Three categories: Shishu, Kishor, and Tarun, based on loan size.

 * No collateral required for loans up to ₹10 lakh.

 * Offered by banks, NBFCs, and MFIs across India.

How to Apply:

Mudra Loans are distributed by commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks, Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), and Micro Financial Institutions (MFIs).

1. Offline Application:

 * Visit a Lending Institution: Go to the nearest branch of a Public/Private Sector Bank, RRB, or MFI that offers Mudra Loans.

 * Complete the Application Form: Fill out the Mudra Loan Application Form. For loans under the Shishu category (up to ₹50,000), a simpler form is often used.

 * Submit Documents: Provide your KYC documents and business proof (see common required documents below).

 * Business Plan: Be ready to present a brief business plan or detail the purpose of the loan.

2. Online Application:

 * Udyamimitra Portal: You can use the official Udyamimitra portal (a platform maintained by SIDBI) to apply online, select a lender, and track your application.

 * Bank Websites: Many large banks allow you to apply directly through their own official website or app under their MSME or small business loan section.

Common Required Documents:

 * Mudra Loan Application Form (duly filled).
 * Identity Proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN card, Passport, etc.).
 * Residence Proof (Electricity bill, Telephone bill, Aadhaar card, etc.).
 * Proof of SC/ST/OBC category, if applicable.
 * Business Proof (Name, address, and proof of existence/running of the business).
 * Bank Statements for the last few months.
 * Quotations for machinery/items to be purchased.

Do Comment If You Have Any Questions 🤔 

#mudraloan #businessloan #governmentyojana #governmentschemes #governmentservices loan

caption: Narendra Modi desh ki bhalayi karne aaya tha aur South African langoti langur ki jihadi chaatugiri politics me fass gaya...Mahatma ban ne ka shortcut doond raha tha. Narendra Das se Mohammed Das ban gaye..!!  Gita baatne aaya tha.. Saugat e Modi baatne lage. Ram ka darbar me Prasad chadaane aaya tha.. Ajmer me chaadar chada baitha. Sab keliye ache din laanewala tha...sirf jihadiyon keliye laakar baitha... Desh ka chowkidari karne wala tha.. Bar dancer parivar ki chowkidari kar baitha...Bharat ma ka mastak jhukne nahi denewala tha, lekin Islami deshon ke samne surrender kar baitha..! Na khavunga.. Na khanedoonga wala sirf khanewalon ko galle lagake baithe..!!  Moun Mohan Sing par tippani katnewala, khud raincoat pahanke nahaane lage..!! Bharat ko Hindu rashtr bananewala Gazwa e Hind walon se besharmi se sone lage... Congress mukt Bharat ka sapna dikhanewala Congress ki chowkidaari kar baitha...khud ko Gareeb fakir kehnewala Air Force One se Ghumare lage.. Armoured imported cars me chamkne lage...Trillions of Swiss bank accounts ka paisa vaapas lakar Bharat ko ameer bananewala, Swiss Bank ka matlab kya hai poochne laga...Hindu par Congress ke dwara kiye gaye anyaayon ko hataane ka pran lenewala khud besharmi se sab ke sab anyayon ko doraane lage...Kashmiri Hindus ko nyaay dilanewala uni Hinduon ko bhool baitha... Secularism ko gaali denewala, secularism ka samardhak ban gaya...Jaativaad hataanewala hindutvavadi, jaativaad ka rajneeti kar baitha...Hindu matt mandiron ki loot ke khilaf chillanewala, Besharmi se loot raha hai mandarin ko 12 saal se...Gulami ka sabhi symbols aur maansikta hataanewala Bharat ko Bharat bulane se darke baitha... Illegal ghusbaithyon par bhashan denewala, ghusbaithyon ka ghar sarkari paise se basane laga... Hindutva ka jhanda buland karaanewala, Sar Tan se juda gang se darke baitha... PoK keliye jaan denewala Bharat ke Veer jawanon ke jaan dete rahe... Laal chowk pe khada hoke jihadiyon ko lalkaarne wala Modi aaj jihadiyon ke godh me baithne laga...desh drohiyon ke saath rajneetik gadhbandhan kar baitha...laanat hai aise beimaanwalon par... Dhikkar hai.. Desh bhakti ka chaadar ke neeche chupe aise desh drohiyon ko desh me koyi jagah nahi honi chahiye... Jai Shri Ram 🙏🙏🙏

Today marks a pivotal moment of self-reflection and determination. The reality is, many people won’t be starting their day by indulging in leftover roses for breakfast, and it’s time to face that truth. Personally, I’ve been without a structured routine for the past three weeks, and today, I’m committed to taking the first step toward reclaiming control.
To kickstart this process, I’ll be fasting today,no food until 8 PM, marking a 24-hour fast. My goal is to maintain an empty stomach, allowing me to reset before returning to the gym. If I feel capable of extending the fast, I will do so, but the key is to listen to my body.
For anyone else struggling with motivation, I suggest you take some time to write down a clear weekly schedule and commit to it. It’s important to establish structure, even if that means dedicating at least one hour each day to yourself,free from distractions like phones or concerns. This time is for you, to recharge mentally and physically.
If you’d like to follow my fitness journey, I’ll be documenting my process openly and transparently, including the supplements I take. While I’m not a professional or qualified to offer advice, I am sharing what has worked for me personally, in the hopes it might inspire or provide insight for others.
Today, I’m also aiming to drink at least 8 glasses of water. Hydration is key, especially when fasting. This is all about consistency, and I’m excited to get back on track #motivation #fyp #fitness #viral #trending. 

And yes I’ll still be reviewing and vlogging life. 
With no drama 😏…

caption:
LOVE ! Just before her Makar Sankranti talk last month, Gurumayi sang Hare Rama Hare Krishna for which she composed the so amazingly beautiful melody, so sweet and so profound, so inspiring.  

Imagine or remember this special 1990 New Year's intensive transmitted worldwide via sattelite for the first time, with sessions on Tapovan hill at the back of Gurudev Siddhapeeth in Ganeshpuri. 

The ashram was so full that huge dormitories tents had been installed everywhere to accomodate everyone. 

Between each act of the Ramayana play, each participant sang this mantra under the stars until late, diving deep into oneself.  

Rama and his beloved Sita, and the love of his brothers; 

Krishna and his beloved Radha and the immense bhakti of the Gopi's for Krishna; 

and now we are on the eve or on the day of Maha Shivaratri's night, honoring Shiva and his beloved Parvati, Shiva-Shakti! 

Let's praise the immense love and patience of Gurumayi for all of us. 

''But you know, I love e-ve-ry-one!''  ~ Gurumayi Chidvilasananda

Our living Guru is so amazingly great! 

And she asks us to think on our own and to act, to do seva for her absolutely without bargain and for the world as well, and to love with respect, to feel the love in our heart. 

''Recharge! Nourish your heart'' ~ Gurumayi Chidvilasananda 1.1.2026

THE WORLD NEEDS our 'prema', and OUR SHAKTI IN ACTION, right now. 

If Bhagawan Nityananda asked Baba Muktananda to initiate the multitude all around the world, it was probably to have enough people everywhere with awakened kundalini and accumulated SHAKTI (spiritual power) to moderate the raging acts of kali yuga at its peak nowadays.

This is why the WORLD NEEDS the MEDITATION REVOLUTION to resume again. 

This is why we have to ‘’Wake up!’’ as said by Gurumayi on Eastern program 2023 (9th April) because "There is one place to sleep: the graveyard! (Until then: wake up)"! 
Not only wake up in Jaya, victory inwardly (we have a lot), but also in Vijaya, in victorious action, in seva. 

And here when Gurumayi uses the term ‘’graveyards’ it’s loaded with meaning as well;
it’s probably to save us from dying sooner than if we act and do the seva she asks us to do (Vijaya) and get the ability to think by our own, droping the deadly conformism to this raging kali yuga (Jaya). It all depends on us now. 

And these are the ACTIONS THAT CAN BE DONE AS SEVA right now, today: 
You can like this page and let see how many we really are to impress them and encourage others to join.

You can join our Indian lawyer sevite (the more, the best). Tell us in Direct Message (DM/(PM)) and we'll connect you to him! 

Keep your dakshina for Gurumayi to finance the cases which will allow Gurumayi to get all back in her hands. Don't give them the dakshina they will use to fight against this. 

You can write letters and e-mails to the trustees - You can use the one example letter (or a part of it) pinned on the top of this page.
You can write a Shivaratri card without an envelope to Gurumayi telling Her how much you love Her and that you are doing the seva She asked for.

You can spread the news that this seva exists since 5th January 2022 to all other devotees you know and try to recruit more sevites at it because the goal is to get the whole sangham at it, probably the best way to get them to listen to Gurumayi. 

You can boycott dakshina to them but put it aside for when it's needed for Gurumayi.
You can boycott their intensive without Gurumayi.
You can even boycott the company of those refusing to hear that this seva exists or don't want to do it. 
You can gather with other sevites doing this seva to create vivid satsangs again of true disciples, the ones listening to Her. 

You can start a case if you are a lawyer; an article or a report if you are a journalist. 
You can approach the human rights of feminists associations or official civil rights organizations, investigating journalists, pro bono advocates, health workers, honest American or Indian politicians. 
You can create a petition. 
You can organize a protest in front of SMA or GSP with a press release the day before. 

You can pray s.y.d.a. people listen to Gurumayi.
 
You can contemplate the situation and think about Gurumayi all the time repeating the mantra, visualizing you and her meeting again, not only inside but in reality in the world, in our ashrams or during programs and retreats to come. 

You can reinforce all the other aspects of your sadhana as well, to give more purity to your seva, giving you even more shakti (power) in your seva. 

Any other creative ideas you may have and also share with us.

And you can think about all the seva you can do as a citizen of this world the way Jaya Lakshmi does it:  
‘she does not bless wealth that enslaves others or hollow growth that erodes values. She represents economic self-reliance guided by ethics—the very spirit of sustainable development and fair growth envisioned in Ātma-Nirbhar Bharat or any other Atma-Nirbhar country or community of the world.’
Let’s all use our immense Shakti the way Gurumayi asks it now!  We all are ’the light of God’, she tells us. So let's it shine in full glory on and on from now on in our independent free way of thinking (Jaya) and our seva for Gurumayi and the world (Vijaya)!

caption:
What Narendra Modi has been able to deliver in such a short span of time, I do not think that anyone else would be able to match this pace.  

Jan Dhan Yojana: Financial inclusion by opening bank accounts for the unbanked, promoting financial literacy and access to credit.

Digital India: A program to improve digital infrastructure, expand internet access, and provide efficient online government services. like UPI payments

Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY): A healthcare initiative providing free health coverage to over 500 million Indians, the largest such scheme globally.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY): A scheme to provide affordable housing for all, with a focus on both urban and rural areas.

Ujjwala Yojana: Free LPG connections to poor households, promoting clean energy and reducing health risks from indoor pollution.

Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY): A scheme providing free ration to the poor during crises like the COVID-19 pandemic, ensuring food security for vulnerable households.

Skill India Mission: A program aimed at providing vocational training to youth to enhance employability and support India’s growing workforce.

PM Kisan Samman Nidhi: Direct income support to small and marginal farmers, providing financial assistance to boost agricultural productivity.

Mission Indradhanush: A nationwide immunization drive to cover all children and pregnant women who have been left out of routine vaccination programs.

Jal Jeevan Mission: A program to provide piped drinking water to every rural household in India by 2024, improving water access and health outcomes.

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi): A scheme offering affordable working capital loans to street vendors, helping them recover and sustain their livelihoods, especially during the pandemic

Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY): A scheme providing financial support through loans to small and micro enterprises, promoting entrepreneurship and self-employment among individuals and small businesses.

Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission): A nationwide campaign for sanitation and eliminating open defecation. This scheme led to the construction of over 110 million toilets across the country.

Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP): A scheme providing affordable, high-quality generic medicines through government-run Janaushadhi Kendras, reducing healthcare costs

Make in India: A program to boost domestic manufacturing and attract foreign investment to make India a global production hub.

Goods and Services Tax (GST): A unified tax reform that simplifies India's indirect tax structure, enhancing ease of business and compliance.

International Solar Alliance (ISA): India's leadership in forming a global coalition to promote solar energy and combat climate change.

Startup India: A scheme to promote entrepreneurship by providing support, ease of doing business, and access to funding for startups.

Beti Bachao Beti Padhao: A campaign to combat gender discrimination, promote education for girls, and improve child sex ratio.

Namami Gange: A project focused on cleaning and rejuvenating the Ganga river, addressing pollution, and restoring its ecological balance.

One Nation, One Ration Card: A scheme to ensure food security for migrant workers by allowing ration card portability across states.

National Education Policy (NEP) 2020: A comprehensive education reform to revamp the curriculum, promote multidisciplinary learning, and improve digital education.

I may have missed another 20 initiatives of this govt which has changed the lives of Indians. NaMo has touched on aspects which no other government had spared any thoughts on it.

Now, the next step step is to enforce Regular Audits and Stricter Compliance of public services.

caption:
Government is working on basics instead of simply announcing freebies like congress! 

1) 2 crore more homes under PM Awas Yojana

2) Housing for middle class

3) Rooftop solar for at least 300 units of power generation which will be free electricity for households

4) Enhancement of target for Lakhpati Didi Scheme from 2 crore women to 3 crore women

5) Preparing and empowering MSMEs to grow and compete globally, aligning regulatory environment for them

6) Making sure that the eastern region becomes the engines of growth for the new Amrit Kaal India

7) Next gen reforms with building consensus with states and stakeholders, for Reform, Perform and Transform

8) Three major railway corridors for logistics efficiency; one corridor lays emphasis on high density passenger traffic route, but at the same time, the corridors will take care of movement of goods as well as that of people; 40,000 bogeys are going to be brought up to the level of Vande Bharat coaches

9) Urbanization, looking at Metro and Namo Bharat, to bring in urban transformation

10) Rs. 1 lakh crore for research and innovation by private sector

11) Boost to tourism, including spiritual tourism, interest-free loans to be given to states so that they can build on iconic tourist centres

12) Supporting reforms in states; there will be a white paper on economic performance of last 10 years compared with previous 10 years. Government has got the trust and confidence of the people based on its exemplary track record on Governance, Development and Performance.

caption:
ಸರ್ಕಾರವೇ ಕೊಡುತ್ತೆ ಸಾಲ! Mudra Loan for Small Business | How to apply, Eligibility,Interest Rates 2025

In this video, we have explained complete information about the Mudra Loan (PMMY) in a simple and easy manner. In 2025, the Mudra Loan limit has been increased from 10 lakhs to 20 lakhs. Learn in detail how much loan you can get under the Shishu, Kishor, Tarun, and the newly added Tarun Plus categories. Here, no collateral is required, the interest rate is low, repayment tenure is 3–7 years, and you also get a moratorium period facility. If you are planning to start a small business like a tea shop, tailoring, transport, or manufacturing, this video is for you.

Resource Link
https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/pmmy
https://www.hdfc.bank.in/pm-mudra-yojana

#mudraloan #pmmy #smallbusinessloan #startupfunding #microenterprise #entrepreneurship #businessfinance #governmentscheme #loanforsmes #financialsupport

Disclaimer: The information provided in this video is only for educational and general awareness purposes. The Mudra Loan is not a government subsidy scheme; any loan you take must be repaid along with the principal and interest. Loan approval depends on the policies of the respective bank or NBFC and their document verification process. Interest rates, repayment period, and moratorium period may vary from one bank to another. The details shared here are based on publicly available information. Before applying for any loan, it is strongly advised to verify all details directly with your bank.

caption:
🇮🇳 प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा लोन योजना की पुरी जानकारी, कमेंट बॉक्स में, फायदा उठाये,#spoanurag #pmmudrayojna #SBI #PNB #trending #short #viral #highlite🇮🇳 प्रधान मंत्री मुद्रा योजना (PMMY) – पूरी जानकारी 2025

शुरुआत: वर्ष 2015
उद्देश्य: छोटे कारोबारियों, नए बिज़नेस, स्टार्टअप, महिलाओं, युवाओं और ग्रामीण उद्यमियों को बिना गारंटी लोन देना।

⭐ मुद्रा लोन क्या है?

यह ऐसा लोन है जिसमें:

कोई गारंटी (Collateral) नहीं लगती

सरकार की गारंटी पर बैंक लोन देता है

इसे MUDRA – Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency के तहत दिया जाता है।

🔥 मुद्रा लोन की 3 कैटेगरी

1️⃣ शिशु लोन — ₹50,000 तक

छोटा काम शुरू करना

फेरीवाला, दूध का काम, छोटी दुकान, टेलरिंग, मोबाइल रिपेयर आदि

2️⃣ किशोर लोन — ₹50,000 से ₹5 लाख तक

दुकान बढ़ाना

मशीनें लेना

छोटे उद्योग लगाना

3️⃣ तरुण लोन — ₹5 लाख से ₹10 लाख तक

बड़ा व्यवसाय

छोटे फैक्ट्री यूनिट

सर्विस सेंटर, ट्रांसपोर्ट, स्टार्टअप 

🎯 कौन-कौन मुद्रा लोन ले सकता है?

✔ छोटे दुकानदार
✔ ट्रांसपोर्टर (ऑटो, टैक्सी, ई-रिक्शा)
✔ मेहंदी/ब्यूटी पार्लर
✔ टेलरिंग/बुटीक
✔ मोबाइल/कंप्यूटर रिपेयर
✔ कृषि आधारित काम
✔ नया बिजनेस शुरू करने वाले
✔ महिलाएँ, युवा, एससी-एसटी
✔ स्टार्टअप

🧾 किन डॉक्यूमेंट की जरूरत है?
1. आधार कार्ड

2. पैन कार्ड

3. फोटो

4. मोबाइल नंबर

5. आधार से लिंक बैंक खाता

6. व्यवसाय का छोटा सा प्रोजेक्ट रिपोर्ट

7. निवास प्रमाण

8. ट्रेड लाइसेंस (जहाँ जरूरी हो)
नोट: गारंटी और सिक्योरिटी की जरूरत नहीं होती।

🏦 कहाँ से मिलेगा मुद्रा लोन?

✔ SBI
✔ PNB
✔ HDFC
✔ ICICI
✔ Bank of Baroda
✔ Cooperative बैंक
✔ Regional Rural Banks
✔ Micro Finance Institutions (MFI)

सभी बैंक मुद्रा लोन देते हैं।

💰 ब्याज दर (Interest Rate)

बैंक के अनुसार अलग होती है।

आमतौर पर 8% से 12% के बीच।

⏳ लोन की अवधि (Repayment Period)

⏳ 3 से 5 साल
कुछ केस में 7 साल तक भी।
⭐ विशेष बातें

महिलाओं को कई बैंक अतिरिक्त लाभ देते हैं

कोई प्रोसेसिंग फीस नहीं

लोन पूरी तरह ट्रांसपेरेंट

बिजनेस शुरू करने वालों को प्राथमिकता
📌 कैसे आवेदन करें?

तरीका 1 – ऑफलाइन

नजदीकी बैंक में जाएँ

“मुद्रा लोन फॉर्म” लें

डॉक्यूमेंट जमा करें

7-15 दिन में मंजूरी
तरीका 2 – ऑनलाइन

PMMY की आधिकारिक साइट पर जाएँ:
➡ (बैंक पोर्टल पर आवेदन करना होता है)
“दोस्तों, अगर आप छोटा बिजनेस शुरू करना चाहते हैं या अपनी दुकान बढ़ाना चाहते हैं तो प्रधान मंत्री मुद्रा योजना आपके लिए सबसे आसान और बड़ा मौका है। इस योजना में आपको 10 लाख तक का लोन बिना किसी गारंटी के मिलता है… ब्याज सामान्य… कागज़ी कार्रवाई आसान… और मंजूरी जल्दी। चाहे आप दुकान चलाते हों, गाड़ी चलाते हों, या कोई नया काम शुरू करना चाहते हों—मुद्रा लोन आपकी मदद करेगा…”

In a small, peaceful town, lived a woman named Maya. She was only 30 years old, but her face showed signs of exhaustion and deep anxiety. For the past few months, Maya had been experiencing strange symptoms—extreme fatigue, stomach pain, and significant weight loss. At first, she ignored the symptoms, thinking it was just stress or normal exhaustion. But as time went on, the symptoms worsened, and eventually, Maya decided to go to the hospital. That day, her mind was filled with tension. She sat in the hospital waiting area, awaiting her test results. Around her, the sounds of people talking about illnesses, diagnoses, and treatments filled the air. It felt like the world had stopped, leaving only worry pressing against her chest. After a while, the doctor called her into the examination room. With a gentle voice, the doctor explained the results of her blood tests and ultrasound, which revealed a mass in Maya’s abdomen. The final diagnosis: likely a malignant tumor. Maya froze, her heart pounding fiercely. It was as if the world was collapsing. Following the diagnosis, Maya needed to undergo a series of additional tests—biopsies, CT scans, and consultations with oncology specialists. The doctor explained that the tumor needed immediate surgery, possibly followed by chemotherapy. Hearing all this, Maya felt her world darken further. But behind the fear, a resolve began to emerge: she had to fight for her life. At the hospital, Maya met a team of caring, professional medical staff. They explained the treatment process patiently, offering reassurance that there was hope—if she was willing to fight. Maya started her treatment, including surgery to remove the tumor and chemotherapy sessions. Each session left scars on her body and her heart, but she tried to stay strong. Throughout this process, Maya battled pain, nausea, and exhaustion. She felt like she was living between hope and fear, trying to keep her spirits up so she wouldn't give in. She also often felt alone, even though her family and friends supported her. During her treatment journey, Maya experienced emotional highs and lows. Sometimes she felt despair, feeling her body was slowly losing its strength. But in those moments, she remembered her doctor’s words and her loved ones’ encouragement: *“You’re not alone, Maya. We’re all here to support you.”* One of the most touching moments was when Maya met another patient also fighting cancer. They shared stories, laughs, and tears. From that, Maya learned that strength doesn’t only come from medication but from courage and the support of loved ones. Additionally, Maya started learning to accept reality. She realized that even though her body was weakening, her spirit had to stay alive. She wrote a letter to herself, expressing her hopes and determination to recover. That letter became a small source of motivation, helping her get up each day. A few months later, her test results showed that the tumor hadn’t completely disappeared. There was a chance that the cancer could become active again, requiring more intensive treatment. The doctor recommended radiation therapy and possibly hospitalization for a few weeks. Maya felt her world growing darker again. She was physically and mentally exhausted. The fear of death was looming over her. She felt tired of fighting, but she also knew that giving up was not an option. She had to keep fighting—for herself and for the people who loved her. During these tough times, her family and friends provided strength. They visited her, cheered her up, and prayed together. Maya realized that her greatest strength came from love and the prayers of those who cared about her. After undergoing a series of exhausting treatments, Maya’s latest check-up showed that the tumor had shrunk significantly. The doctor delivered good news: the cancer could be controlled, and she was likely to recover. Maya felt tears streaming down her cheeks. She felt reborn. Her fight hadn’t been in vain. She realized that her greatest strength came from within herself, from her bravery and her refusal to give up. After months of recovery, Maya began to live a normal life again. She went back to work, resumed her activities, and even started practicing yoga and meditation to maintain emotional balance. She also became active in sharing her experience with others fighting similar battles, as a way to give back and inspire hope.
This story ends with a powerful message: although the journey fighting illness is tough and filled with challenges, hope always exists. No matter how dark the world seems, inner strength and the support of loved ones can bring about miracles.
On a sunny day, Maya stood in a park, gazing at the sky and smiling. She knew life was full of uncertainties, but as long as there was hope, anything was possible. She promised to live each day with gratitude and courage, welcoming a future full of hope.
This story teaches us that going to the hospital isn’t just about physical treatment; it’s about courage, hope, and mental strength. Maya’s journey is a reflection of human resilience in facing difficult times. content:
In a small, peaceful town, lived a woman named Maya. She was only 30 years old, but her face showed signs of exhaustion and deep anxiety. For the past few months, Maya had been experiencing strange symptoms—extreme fatigue, stomach pain, and significant weight loss. At first, she ignored the symptoms, thinking it was just stress or normal exhaustion. But as time went on, the symptoms worsened, and eventually, Maya decided to go to the hospital. That day, her mind was filled with tension. She sat in the hospital waiting area, awaiting her test results. Around her, the sounds of people talking about illnesses, diagnoses, and treatments filled the air. It felt like the world had stopped, leaving only worry pressing against her chest. After a while, the doctor called her into the examination room. With a gentle voice, the doctor explained the results of her blood tests and ultrasound, which revealed a mass in Maya’s abdomen. The final diagnosis: likely a malignant tumor. Maya froze, her heart pounding fiercely. It was as if the world was collapsing. Following the diagnosis, Maya needed to undergo a series of additional tests—biopsies, CT scans, and consultations with oncology specialists. The doctor explained that the tumor needed immediate surgery, possibly followed by chemotherapy. Hearing all this, Maya felt her world darken further. But behind the fear, a resolve began to emerge: she had to fight for her life. At the hospital, Maya met a team of caring, professional medical staff. They explained the treatment process patiently, offering reassurance that there was hope—if she was willing to fight. Maya started her treatment, including surgery to remove the tumor and chemotherapy sessions. Each session left scars on her body and her heart, but she tried to stay strong. Throughout this process, Maya battled pain, nausea, and exhaustion. She felt like she was living between hope and fear, trying to keep her spirits up so she wouldn't give in. She also often felt alone, even though her family and friends supported her. During her treatment journey, Maya experienced emotional highs and lows. Sometimes she felt despair, feeling her body was slowly losing its strength. But in those moments, she remembered her doctor’s words and her loved ones’ encouragement: *“You’re not alone, Maya. We’re all here to support you.”* One of the most touching moments was when Maya met another patient also fighting cancer. They shared stories, laughs, and tears. From that, Maya learned that strength doesn’t only come from medication but from courage and the support of loved ones. Additionally, Maya started learning to accept reality. She realized that even though her body was weakening, her spirit had to stay alive. She wrote a letter to herself, expressing her hopes and determination to recover. That letter became a small source of motivation, helping her get up each day. A few months later, her test results showed that the tumor hadn’t completely disappeared. There was a chance that the cancer could become active again, requiring more intensive treatment. The doctor recommended radiation therapy and possibly hospitalization for a few weeks. Maya felt her world growing darker again. She was physically and mentally exhausted. The fear of death was looming over her. She felt tired of fighting, but she also knew that giving up was not an option. She had to keep fighting—for herself and for the people who loved her. During these tough times, her family and friends provided strength. They visited her, cheered her up, and prayed together. Maya realized that her greatest strength came from love and the prayers of those who cared about her. After undergoing a series of exhausting treatments, Maya’s latest check-up showed that the tumor had shrunk significantly. The doctor delivered good news: the cancer could be controlled, and she was likely to recover. Maya felt tears streaming down her cheeks. She felt reborn. Her fight hadn’t been in vain. She realized that her greatest strength came from within herself, from her bravery and her refusal to give up. After months of recovery, Maya began to live a normal life again. She went back to work, resumed her activities, and even started practicing yoga and meditation to maintain emotional balance. She also became active in sharing her experience with others fighting similar battles, as a way to give back and inspire hope.
This story ends with a powerful message: although the journey fighting illness is tough and filled with challenges, hope always exists. No matter how dark the world seems, inner strength and the support of loved ones can bring about miracles.
On a sunny day, Maya stood in a park, gazing at the sky and smiling. She knew life was full of uncertainties, but as long as there was hope, anything was possible. She promised to live each day with gratitude and courage, welcoming a future full of hope.
This story teaches us that going to the hospital isn’t just about physical treatment; it’s about courage, hope, and mental strength. Maya’s journey is a reflection of human resilience in facing difficult times. post_content.caption:
In a small, peaceful town, lived a woman named Maya. She was only 30 years old, but her face showed signs of exhaustion and deep anxiety. For the past few months, Maya had been experiencing strange symptoms—extreme fatigue, stomach pain, and significant weight loss. At first, she ignored the symptoms, thinking it was just stress or normal exhaustion. But as time went on, the symptoms worsened, and eventually, Maya decided to go to the hospital. That day, her mind was filled with tension. She sat in the hospital waiting area, awaiting her test results. Around her, the sounds of people talking about illnesses, diagnoses, and treatments filled the air. It felt like the world had stopped, leaving only worry pressing against her chest. After a while, the doctor called her into the examination room. With a gentle voice, the doctor explained the results of her blood tests and ultrasound, which revealed a mass in Maya’s abdomen. The final diagnosis: likely a malignant tumor. Maya froze, her heart pounding fiercely. It was as if the world was collapsing. Following the diagnosis, Maya needed to undergo a series of additional tests—biopsies, CT scans, and consultations with oncology specialists. The doctor explained that the tumor needed immediate surgery, possibly followed by chemotherapy. Hearing all this, Maya felt her world darken further. But behind the fear, a resolve began to emerge: she had to fight for her life. At the hospital, Maya met a team of caring, professional medical staff. They explained the treatment process patiently, offering reassurance that there was hope—if she was willing to fight. Maya started her treatment, including surgery to remove the tumor and chemotherapy sessions. Each session left scars on her body and her heart, but she tried to stay strong. Throughout this process, Maya battled pain, nausea, and exhaustion. She felt like she was living between hope and fear, trying to keep her spirits up so she wouldn't give in. She also often felt alone, even though her family and friends supported her. During her treatment journey, Maya experienced emotional highs and lows. Sometimes she felt despair, feeling her body was slowly losing its strength. But in those moments, she remembered her doctor’s words and her loved ones’ encouragement: *“You’re not alone, Maya. We’re all here to support you.”* One of the most touching moments was when Maya met another patient also fighting cancer. They shared stories, laughs, and tears. From that, Maya learned that strength doesn’t only come from medication but from courage and the support of loved ones. Additionally, Maya started learning to accept reality. She realized that even though her body was weakening, her spirit had to stay alive. She wrote a letter to herself, expressing her hopes and determination to recover. That letter became a small source of motivation, helping her get up each day. A few months later, her test results showed that the tumor hadn’t completely disappeared. There was a chance that the cancer could become active again, requiring more intensive treatment. The doctor recommended radiation therapy and possibly hospitalization for a few weeks. Maya felt her world growing darker again. She was physically and mentally exhausted. The fear of death was looming over her. She felt tired of fighting, but she also knew that giving up was not an option. She had to keep fighting—for herself and for the people who loved her. During these tough times, her family and friends provided strength. They visited her, cheered her up, and prayed together. Maya realized that her greatest strength came from love and the prayers of those who cared about her. After undergoing a series of exhausting treatments, Maya’s latest check-up showed that the tumor had shrunk significantly. The doctor delivered good news: the cancer could be controlled, and she was likely to recover. Maya felt tears streaming down her cheeks. She felt reborn. Her fight hadn’t been in vain. She realized that her greatest strength came from within herself, from her bravery and her refusal to give up. After months of recovery, Maya began to live a normal life again. She went back to work, resumed her activities, and even started practicing yoga and meditation to maintain emotional balance. She also became active in sharing her experience with others fighting similar battles, as a way to give back and inspire hope.
This story ends with a powerful message: although the journey fighting illness is tough and filled with challenges, hope always exists. No matter how dark the world seems, inner strength and the support of loved ones can bring about miracles.
On a sunny day, Maya stood in a park, gazing at the sky and smiling. She knew life was full of uncertainties, but as long as there was hope, anything was possible. She promised to live each day with gratitude and courage, welcoming a future full of hope.
This story teaches us that going to the hospital isn’t just about physical treatment; it’s about courage, hope, and mental strength. Maya’s journey is a reflection of human resilience in facing difficult times. caption:
***Stonepeak bought a 50-percent share of Dominion’s CVOW***
Stonepeak’s Synera Seeks $800 Million Loan for Taiwan Wind Farm
By Megawati Wijaya
February 12, 2026 at 10:52 PM EST

Synera Renewable Energy Co., a portfolio company of Stonepeak Partners, is seeking $800 million of private credit for its offshore wind farm project in Taiwan, according to people familiar with the matter, amid the push for green power supply expansion in the country.

Proceeds from the proposed loan will be used to fund the construction and ramp-up of the Formosa 2 offshore wind farm project, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the proposed deal is private. Stonepeak declined to comment. Synera did not respond to a request for comment.

Taiwanese Vice Premier Cheng Li-chiun earlier this year instructed government ministries to continue strengthening green finance support for offshore wind power projects, according to a cabinet statement. Offshore wind power development is expected to require around NT$2 trillion ($64 billion) in funding by 2035, the statement said.

Located off the coast of Miaoli County in Taiwan, Formosa 2 has an installed capacity of 376 MW, and has signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Taiwan Power Company, according to a website.

caption:
Shenandoah Downs Spring Meet Racing Applications Available Beginning February 2 

Shenandoah Downs will usher in its 11th year of pari-mutuel harness racing April 11 and continue a 7-week spring meet thru May 24 with programs every Saturday & Sunday at 1:05 PM. A 7-week fall meet will follow and extend from September 19 - November 1. Dates for both campaigns were formally approved by the Virginia Racing Commission at its December meeting. 

Racing applications for the spring session will be available at shenandoahdowns.com beginning February 2 and need to be submitted to the race office by March 11. Peter Szymanski enters year number three in his role as Director of Racing and Karen Fagliarone returns for her second year as Racing Secretary. For more details, horsemen can contact Karen at 732-239-0281 or e-mail her at raceoffice@shenandoahdowns.com. 

The barn area opens Monday April 6 and pre-meet qualifiers will be offered on Tuesday April 7 at 10 AM.  After that date, qualifiers will take place on Saturdays at 12 Noon --- including opening day, April 11. Racing entries will be taken every Wednesday for both weekend race cards. Saturday entries will clear on Thursday and Sunday's will clear on Friday. 

Shenandoah Downs will experiment by going with seven horse fields this spring whenever possible (in non-stakes races) as a new safety initiative. 

A new multi-leg Seven Bends Claiming Series --- celebrating the seven bends of the Shenandoah River that wind through Woodstock --- will be formalized in the coming days and posted on the track website.            

Virginia Sire Stake and Breeder's Fund eliminations and finals for 3-year-olds will take place during the spring season. Sire Stake trot eliminations (April 18) and pace eliminations (April 19) will lead up to $60,000 final rounds --- for both gaits --- on April 25. Three-year-old trot eliminations on (May 9, 16) and pace eliminations (May 10, 17) will lead up to $80,000 final rounds --- for both gaits --- on May 23. 

A single round of $20,000 Breeders Fund Aged trot and pace events will be conducted on May 2. Virginia Breeder's and Sire Stake events for two-year-olds will take place in the fall meet. 

Shenandoah Downs will continue to make use of its new 175-stall, 32,500 square foot horse barn which debuted last fall. The Virginia Equine Alliance funded the $2 million project to create a permanent structure to safely house horses during both meets. Two additional smaller barns are utilized as well along with 60 ship-in stalls.

Shenandoah Downs is conveniently located in Woodstock, Virginia halfway between Winchester and Harrisonburg at I-81, Exit 283 --- in the heart of the Shenandoah Valley. The Shenandoah County Fair is held there every summer and includes a four-day non-wagering harness meet which in 2026, will run from September 2-5.

It was a typical Monday morning at Maplewood Elementary School. The classroom buzzed with energy as students settled into their seats, chatting about weekend plans and last night's TV shows. Among them was Ethan, an 11-year-old boy who always seemed to be in his own world. His clothes were worn-out and too big for him, and his hair was often unruly. Ethan rarely spoke in class, preferring to keep to himself. Throughout the day, Ethan’s classmates often teased him, calling him an "inventor" in a mocking tone. They laughed at his old clothes, his quiet demeanor, and his tendency to stay alone during breaks. No one really knew much about Ethan—he kept his distance, and nobody tried to get to know him. That day, the teacher, Mrs. Carter, decided to change things up. Instead of the usual lesson, she asked the students to talk about their parents’ professions. She went around the room, asking each child to share what their parents did for a living. One by one, students proudly announced their parents’ jobs. “My mom is a lawyer,” said Sarah. “My dad runs an IT company,” added James. When it was Ethan’s turn, Mrs. Carter looked at him expectantly. Ethan hesitated, then remained silent. The teacher, slightly puzzled, asked again, “Ethan, what do your parents do?” Ethan looked down at his desk, fidgeting nervously. Finally, he whispered, “My parents don’t work.” A sudden silence fell over the classroom. Then, a ripple of laughter erupted. The students looked at each other, whispering and giggling. Mrs. Carter’s eyebrows raised in surprise, and she couldn’t help but chuckle a little, though she quickly regained her composure. “That’s why you always come to school in old and worn-out clothes,” Mrs. Carter said with a teasing smile, not realizing how hurtful her words were. The classroom erupted in louder laughter. Ethan’s face turned red, tears welling up in his eyes. His shoulders trembled as he tried to hold back sobs. He felt humiliated, ashamed, and completely alone in that moment.
Just as the laughter reached its peak, the classroom door swung open with a sudden gust of wind. Standing in the doorway was a man Ethan had never seen before—his face stern yet kind. His eyes swept across the room, taking in the scene. Everyone fell silent. The man stepped inside slowly, his gaze fixed on Ethan. The boy looked up, eyes wide with fear and curiosity. The man knelt beside Ethan and gently placed his hand on the boy’s shoulder. “Ethan,” he said softly, “may I have a moment?” . Mrs. Carter looked surprised but nodded. The man turned to the class and said, “I think the boy you’re teasing has a story you all need to hear.”Ethan’s eyes shimmered with tears. He looked at the man, then back at his classmates, and finally gathered the courage to speak. “My name is Ethan,” he whispered. “My parents... they don’t work because they’re not like other parents. My father is a scientist, and my mother is an inventor. They don’t have a big company or fancy jobs, but they make things. They build gadgets and invent new ideas. They’re the reason I love to create things, even if I don’t have nice clothes or a lot of money. I want to be like them someday.” Silence filled the room. The classmates stared at Ethan in awe, unsure of what to say. The teacher looked at the man, who nodded approvingly. The man then turned to the class. “Ethan’s parents are inventors,” he said. “They work quietly, but their inventions change lives in ways you might never see. Sometimes, greatness isn’t about wealth or fame, but about making the world a better place in your own way.” The class was silent, absorbing his words. Ethan looked down, clutching his backpack tightly. The man stood up and looked at Ethan kindly. “You’re special, Ethan. Never be ashamed of who you are. Your parents’ work is important, and so are you.”
As he spoke, something shifted in the classroom. The teasing stopped. The children looked at Ethan with new respect and curiosity. Mrs. Carter, feeling guilty for her earlier words, approached Ethan with a gentle smile. “I’m sorry I teased you, Ethan,” she said softly. “Your story is inspiring. I think we all have something to learn from you.” Ethan’s tears slowly dried, and a faint smile appeared on his face. For the first time, he felt seen—not as the boy with old clothes and no parents, but as a young inventor with a bright future. Later that day, Ethan stayed after school with the man. They talked about ideas, inventions, and dreams. Ethan realized that even though his family was different, their work was meaningful. He felt a newfound confidence swelling inside him. From that day on, Ethan’s classmates no longer teased him. Instead, they looked up to him, eager to learn about his inventions and dreams. Ethan continued to create, inspired by his parents’ silent work and the newfound respect he earned. And somewhere, in a small workshop at home, Ethan’s parents smiled quietly, proud of their son’s courage and the new path he was about to forge.   Sometimes, the most extraordinary stories come from the quietest places. It was a typical Monday morning at Maplewood Elementary School. The classroom buzzed with energy as students settled into their seats, chatting about weekend plans and last night's TV shows. Among them was Ethan, an 11-year-old boy who always seemed to be in his own world. His clothes were worn-out and too big for him, and his hair was often unruly. Ethan rarely spoke in class, preferring to keep to himself. Throughout the day, Ethan’s classmates often teased him, calling him an "inventor" in a mocking tone. They laughed at his old clothes, his quiet demeanor, and his tendency to stay alone during breaks. No one really knew much about Ethan—he kept his distance, and nobody tried to get to know him. That day, the teacher, Mrs. Carter, decided to change things up. Instead of the usual lesson, she asked the students to talk about their parents’ professions. She went around the room, asking each child to share what their parents did for a living. One by one, students proudly announced their parents’ jobs. “My mom is a lawyer,” said Sarah. “My dad runs an IT company,” added James. When it was Ethan’s turn, Mrs. Carter looked at him expectantly. Ethan hesitated, then remained silent. The teacher, slightly puzzled, asked again, “Ethan, what do your parents do?” Ethan looked down at his desk, fidgeting nervously. Finally, he whispered, “My parents don’t work.” A sudden silence fell over the classroom. Then, a ripple of laughter erupted. The students looked at each other, whispering and giggling. Mrs. Carter’s eyebrows raised in surprise, and she couldn’t help but chuckle a little, though she quickly regained her composure. “That’s why you always come to school in old and worn-out clothes,” Mrs. Carter said with a teasing smile, not realizing how hurtful her words were. The classroom erupted in louder laughter. Ethan’s face turned red, tears welling up in his eyes. His shoulders trembled as he tried to hold back sobs. He felt humiliated, ashamed, and completely alone in that moment.
Just as the laughter reached its peak, the classroom door swung open with a sudden gust of wind. Standing in the doorway was a man Ethan had never seen before—his face stern yet kind. His eyes swept across the room, taking in the scene. Everyone fell silent. The man stepped inside slowly, his gaze fixed on Ethan. The boy looked up, eyes wide with fear and curiosity. The man knelt beside Ethan and gently placed his hand on the boy’s shoulder. “Ethan,” he said softly, “may I have a moment?” . Mrs. Carter looked surprised but nodded. The man turned to the class and said, “I think the boy you’re teasing has a story you all need to hear.”Ethan’s eyes shimmered with tears. He looked at the man, then back at his classmates, and finally gathered the courage to speak. “My name is Ethan,” he whispered. “My parents... they don’t work because they’re not like other parents. My father is a scientist, and my mother is an inventor. They don’t have a big company or fancy jobs, but they make things. They build gadgets and invent new ideas. They’re the reason I love to create things, even if I don’t have nice clothes or a lot of money. I want to be like them someday.” Silence filled the room. The classmates stared at Ethan in awe, unsure of what to say. The teacher looked at the man, who nodded approvingly. The man then turned to the class. “Ethan’s parents are inventors,” he said. “They work quietly, but their inventions change lives in ways you might never see. Sometimes, greatness isn’t about wealth or fame, but about making the world a better place in your own way.” The class was silent, absorbing his words. Ethan looked down, clutching his backpack tightly. The man stood up and looked at Ethan kindly. “You’re special, Ethan. Never be ashamed of who you are. Your parents’ work is important, and so are you.”
As he spoke, something shifted in the classroom. The teasing stopped. The children looked at Ethan with new respect and curiosity. Mrs. Carter, feeling guilty for her earlier words, approached Ethan with a gentle smile. “I’m sorry I teased you, Ethan,” she said softly. “Your story is inspiring. I think we all have something to learn from you.” Ethan’s tears slowly dried, and a faint smile appeared on his face. For the first time, he felt seen—not as the boy with old clothes and no parents, but as a young inventor with a bright future. Later that day, Ethan stayed after school with the man. They talked about ideas, inventions, and dreams. Ethan realized that even though his family was different, their work was meaningful. He felt a newfound confidence swelling inside him. From that day on, Ethan’s classmates no longer teased him. Instead, they looked up to him, eager to learn about his inventions and dreams. Ethan continued to create, inspired by his parents’ silent work and the newfound respect he earned. And somewhere, in a small workshop at home, Ethan’s parents smiled quietly, proud of their son’s courage and the new path he was about to forge.   Sometimes, the most extraordinary stories come from the quietest places. It was a typical Monday morning at Maplewood Elementary School. The classroom buzzed with energy as students settled into their seats, chatting about weekend plans and last night's TV shows. Among them was Ethan, an 11-year-old boy who always seemed to be in his own world. His clothes were worn-out and too big for him, and his hair was often unruly. Ethan rarely spoke in class, preferring to keep to himself. Throughout the day, Ethan’s classmates often teased him, calling him an "inventor" in a mocking tone. They laughed at his old clothes, his quiet demeanor, and his tendency to stay alone during breaks. No one really knew much about Ethan—he kept his distance, and nobody tried to get to know him. That day, the teacher, Mrs. Carter, decided to change things up. Instead of the usual lesson, she asked the students to talk about their parents’ professions. She went around the room, asking each child to share what their parents did for a living. One by one, students proudly announced their parents’ jobs. “My mom is a lawyer,” said Sarah. “My dad runs an IT company,” added James. When it was Ethan’s turn, Mrs. Carter looked at him expectantly. Ethan hesitated, then remained silent. The teacher, slightly puzzled, asked again, “Ethan, what do your parents do?” Ethan looked down at his desk, fidgeting nervously. Finally, he whispered, “My parents don’t work.” A sudden silence fell over the classroom. Then, a ripple of laughter erupted. The students looked at each other, whispering and giggling. Mrs. Carter’s eyebrows raised in surprise, and she couldn’t help but chuckle a little, though she quickly regained her composure. “That’s why you always come to school in old and worn-out clothes,” Mrs. Carter said with a teasing smile, not realizing how hurtful her words were. The classroom erupted in louder laughter. Ethan’s face turned red, tears welling up in his eyes. His shoulders trembled as he tried to hold back sobs. He felt humiliated, ashamed, and completely alone in that moment.
Just as the laughter reached its peak, the classroom door swung open with a sudden gust of wind. Standing in the doorway was a man Ethan had never seen before—his face stern yet kind. His eyes swept across the room, taking in the scene. Everyone fell silent. The man stepped inside slowly, his gaze fixed on Ethan. The boy looked up, eyes wide with fear and curiosity. The man knelt beside Ethan and gently placed his hand on the boy’s shoulder. “Ethan,” he said softly, “may I have a moment?” . Mrs. Carter looked surprised but nodded. The man turned to the class and said, “I think the boy you’re teasing has a story you all need to hear.”Ethan’s eyes shimmered with tears. He looked at the man, then back at his classmates, and finally gathered the courage to speak. “My name is Ethan,” he whispered. “My parents... they don’t work because they’re not like other parents. My father is a scientist, and my mother is an inventor. They don’t have a big company or fancy jobs, but they make things. They build gadgets and invent new ideas. They’re the reason I love to create things, even if I don’t have nice clothes or a lot of money. I want to be like them someday.” Silence filled the room. The classmates stared at Ethan in awe, unsure of what to say. The teacher looked at the man, who nodded approvingly. The man then turned to the class. “Ethan’s parents are inventors,” he said. “They work quietly, but their inventions change lives in ways you might never see. Sometimes, greatness isn’t about wealth or fame, but about making the world a better place in your own way.” The class was silent, absorbing his words. Ethan looked down, clutching his backpack tightly. The man stood up and looked at Ethan kindly. “You’re special, Ethan. Never be ashamed of who you are. Your parents’ work is important, and so are you.”
As he spoke, something shifted in the classroom. The teasing stopped. The children looked at Ethan with new respect and curiosity. Mrs. Carter, feeling guilty for her earlier words, approached Ethan with a gentle smile. “I’m sorry I teased you, Ethan,” she said softly. “Your story is inspiring. I think we all have something to learn from you.” Ethan’s tears slowly dried, and a faint smile appeared on his face. For the first time, he felt seen—not as the boy with old clothes and no parents, but as a young inventor with a bright future. Later that day, Ethan stayed after school with the man. They talked about ideas, inventions, and dreams. Ethan realized that even though his family was different, their work was meaningful. He felt a newfound confidence swelling inside him. From that day on, Ethan’s classmates no longer teased him. Instead, they looked up to him, eager to learn about his inventions and dreams. Ethan continued to create, inspired by his parents’ silent work and the newfound respect he earned. And somewhere, in a small workshop at home, Ethan’s parents smiled quietly, proud of their son’s courage and the new path he was about to forge.   Sometimes, the most extraordinary stories come from the quietest places.
