*ANDREW NEIL: The evidence suggests this will be a year of economic revival that could lift Britain out of its gloom. But this is why I predict Starmer and Reeves will screw it all up yet again... and be kicked out of office*

On this first day of 2026, let us start with some surprising New Year cheer: prospects for the British economy look better than they have for quite some time.

A number of global developments are set to unfold in the coming year which together could lift us out of our current economic slough of despond.

The gravest risk to this rosy scenario is, of course, the dead hands of Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves – all the more dangerous when coupled with the congenital economic ignorance of today’s Labour Party. 

Together they could snuff out any green shoots of recovery before they have a chance to flourish, just as they did in 2025, a miserable year for the economy under Labour’s enterprise-sapping tutelage.

None of the good economic news set to grace our shores in 2026 has much to do with Starmer-Reeves. It will happen despite them – above all the rapidly growing global glut of oil and gas, which will exert substantial and welcome downward pressure on energy prices.
Despite weakening demand for oil, the Saudis are pumping out more and more of the black stuff to regain global market share. The US is over-drilling too, encouraged by Donald Trump’s ‘drill, baby, drill’ exhortations.

The International Energy Agency reckons demand for oil will rise by 1.6million barrels per day in 2026. But production will increase by almost 6million barrels, even without Russia re-entering official oil markets. 

Such a huge increase in supply over demand can only mean one thing: oil prices will continue to fall in 2026, perhaps quite dramatically.

The same is true for natural gas. The wholesale price of gas in Europe is already close to pre-Ukraine war levels. 

Yet Trump is still pushing to turn America into the world’s biggest exporter of liquified natural gas (LNG) – sent as frozen liquid in massive ships across the globe. America’s capacity to export LNG is on track to increase tenfold in this decade.

This huge expansion is taking place just as several major markets are cutting their use of gas. China is rolling out massive new wind and solar electricity-generating capacity because it wishes to reduce its dependence on shipborne energy supplies, which it fears could be too easily disrupted by the US Navy.

Chinese LNG imports fell almost 20 percent in 2025 – not one LNG tanker from America has docked in a Chinese port for almost a year – and will decline further in 2026. India, Thailand and even Pakistan (where farmers and factories are installing cheap Chinese solar panels on a massive scale) are also reducing their appetite for LNG.

As with oil, surging supply of gas coupled with weakening demand for it can only mean one thing: the price of gas continues to fall, perhaps even to plummet.

The economic significance of falling energy prices in 2026 will be immense – the equivalent of a £1trillion stimulus for the oil-and-gas guzzling economies of Europe, including the UK. Not before time.

The British economy is stuck in a stagnant rut in which growth of 1.5 per cent is regarded as close to boom times. The Eurozone is faring no better. Cheaper energy this year could be just the boost Europe and the UK need to pump some life back into their economies.

But the good news doesn’t stop there – and once again China will play a pivotal role. A new wave of cheap Chinese imports – everything from electric vehicles, batteries and solar panels to machinery, steel and chemicals – will swamp the world economy this year.

Given Trump’s tariffs have somewhat closed off America, Europe and the UK are now their premier destination. 

This is not good news for what’s left of our industrial base. But it will result in the defeat of inflation in 2026 by exerting serious downward pressure on prices – ‘disinflation’ in the jargon – which is especially significant for Britain.
Eurozone inflation is already pretty much on target at two per cent and set to fall further; it’s under three per cent in America. 

But we came close to four per cent earlier this year, thanks to the Starmer-Reeves addiction to borrowing, high taxes and big wage rises, all of which pushed up prices. UK inflation is only now falling back towards three per cent again.

Chinese disinflation will push UK prices down further. I expect us to hit the official two per cent inflation target (at last) before spring is out. That will pave the way for further cuts in interest rates in 2026, which will be good news for households with a mortgage and small companies who’ve borrowed to expand.

The Bank of England, which has been wary of cutting interest rates too fast or by too much because our inflation is the highest in the G7 club of the biggest market economies, will find safety in numbers when it comes to further rate cuts.

The US Federal Reserve benchmark interest rate is currently 3.75 per cent. I expect that to fall to three per cent this year, propelled downwards by a new Fed chairman more likely to do 

Trump’s bidding when it comes to cheap money.
The UK benchmark rate is also 3.75 per cent. Lower inflation will allow us to follow in the Fed’s footsteps towards three per cent. The Eurozone benchmark rate is already two per cent. That probably won’t change. But if it does, it will be down, not up.

Falling inflation followed by more cuts in interest rates are another reason to be cautiously cheerful about the economy in 2026. There’s one more – rearmament, another potential stimulus to the economy.

The Germans are leading the way in Europe with a massive boost to defence spending from a low base. The Poles and Scandinavians are also doing their bit to deter a revanchist Russia from further military adventures with stronger defences.

But Britain is a laggard. Our government talks a lot about extra defence spending but seems to have mislaid its cheque book.

We will spend very little more on rearming in 2026 than we did in 2025 – yet another failure of the Starmer-Reeves government. The military and economic case for a major boost to defence spending is overwhelming. The UK government needs to get on with it.

Falling energy prices. Lower inflation. Falling mortgage rates. More defence spending. Together they amount to a real opportunity to break out of the economic doldrums. What could possibly go wrong? Easy: Starmer-Reeves.

In the summer of 2024 they inherited the fastest-growing economy in the G7. For a while the new government was carried along by that momentum. But the wrecking ball of its first Budget in November 2024 took its toll in 2025.
Growth went from a respectable 0.7 per cent in the first quarter of last year to a worrying 0.3 per cent in the second, a pathetic 0.1 per cent in the third – and a likely stagnant 0.0 per cent in the fourth quarter just ended.

But the sad catalogue of Starmer-Reeves failures doesn’t stop with a slump in growth. It includes higher inflation, rising unemployment (4.4 per cent a year ago, now over 5 per cent), the lowest investment of any G7 economy and reckless borrowing.

The Tories borrowed an incredible £311billion in 2020-21 to counter the impact of the pandemic. Labour wanted them to borrow even more. But within a year the Tories were getting a post-pandemic grip on the public finances: borrowing fell to £120billion in 2021-22.

Labour promptly reversed that: borrowing soared back to £153billion in 2024-25 and looks like being roughly the same in the current financial year.

So, even with some good economic news coming round the corner, what is to stop Starmer-Reeves screwing it up all over again in 2026? Especially since, to save their skins, they are now in thrall to Labour’s soft Left, which has become the dominant force in the party and which wants to borrow, spend and tax more.
Of course, neither might be around for long enough to make a second hash of things.

I have covered the troubles of many previous prime ministers as their party fell out of love with them – from Ted Heath way back in the early 1970s to Margaret Thatcher in the late 1980s, John Major in the 1990s and Tony Blair and Gordon Brown in the first decade of this century. But I have never witnessed anything like the visceral dislike – bordering on hatred – that Labour backbenchers have for Starmer (and, by extension, Reeves).

The settled Labour consensus is that he’s a dud – as useless at politics as he is at policy, twin defects that were amply on display this week after he welcomed an Egyptian activist to our shores, seemingly unaware he was an anti-Semitic, anti-British, anti-white extremist with a violent streak. That had even the PM’s cabinet ministers shaking their heads in despair.

Labour MPs have been biding their time waiting to ditch Starmer after the May elections, which are universally expected to be a disaster for him in England (at least in those parts where Labour is allowing elections), Scotland and Wales. But a growing number are no longer prepared to wait that long: they want to dump him as soon as possible.

This is not necessarily good news for the economy. The bond markets, where governments go to borrow, fear any change at the top would result in an even more Left-wing government. 

They’re right: all potential successors are to Starmer’s Left, bar Health Secretary Wes Streeting – and even he’s tilting that way to curry favour with the soft Left. Manchester Mayor Andy Burham, who doesn’t hide his leadership ambitions, complains about Labour being ‘in hock’ to the bond markets: there’s a simple way to avoid that, Andy — stop borrowing so much from them!

An Angela Rayner government (perish the thought) is hardly likely to be a pinnacle of fiscal rectitude. Ditto one led by Ed Miliband (another perishing thought).

The above three and several more, spent much of 2025 on manoeuvres to replace Starmer. They will pick up where they left off in the New Year, with renewed vigour. The danger for the UK economy is that, in response to these Labour Party machinations indicating a clear lean to the Left, the bond markets decide to dump British debt, forcing up government borrowing costs to unaffordable levels.

That would be the modern equivalent of the 1976 economic crisis under a previous Labour government, which led to the humiliation of being bailed out by the International Monetary Fund. But history doesn’t quite repeat itself.
Rather than a second IMF bailout, the British government would more likely be left to retrench on its own, forced to slash spending and raise taxes because it had run out of room to borrow any more. It would make the so-called austerity of the Cameron-Osborne years look like the good times and split Labour asunder.

I do not predict such a cataclysm for 2026 (though I wouldn’t entirely rule it out either). But if anything is likely to provoke the notorious bond vigilantes to do their worst this year it is the prospect of an even more profligate Labour government than the Starmer-Reeves regime.
It would certainly overwhelm all the potential good economic news that awaits us this year – and it speaks volumes for our current predicament that the best international investors can see for us is a continuation of Starmer-Reeves. Truly blessed we are not.

Compared with Starmer’s ‘end of days’, Kemi Badenoch starts 2026 in much better shape than she began last year. The Tory leader has gained in confidence, come across as the decent person she is and often bested a flat-footed Starmer at Prime Minister’s Questions.
Her (perhaps insurmountable) problem is that she heads a political brand which could be tarnished beyond rescue and which has haemorrhaged support to Reform, which might not be reclaimable.

That said, Reform ended 2025 slipping a little in the polls having peaked at just over 30 per cent (while the Tories started to gain a few points from a very low base) and with a sense in some quarters that Nigel Farage had somewhat lost his mojo. He and his party certainly no longer dominate the national discourse the way they did for much of last year.

We will find out soon enough in 2026 if the Tory revival is real or if Reform quickly bounds back to establish its credentials as the new and dominant party of the Right. Only one or the other can happen – not both. For Starmer there are no good prospects. Even if he survives until the May elections the results will be dismal for him.

Labour will lose control of the Welsh Parliament, which it has run since the latter was established in 1998. A year ago Labour was poised to take the Scottish Parliament. Now, thanks to Starmer’s deep unpopularity north of the border, the SNP will hold on to power and Labour could come third (behind the SNP and even Reform).
While Reform could be given a new lease of life with a strong showing in England’s local elections in May, Labour will continue to shed its Left base to the Greens and their glib new leader.

I started off with some good cheer for the New Year. My fear is good economic prospects will be more than thwarted by bad politics. Starmer and Reeves will be brought down by their own socialist conceit: that economic growth can be fostered by a bigger public sector, higher taxes, more public spending.

It can’t. In fact, that’s how you stifle growth. But, amazingly, as both are dispatched to the wilderness for failing, Labour will double down on its socialist fantasies –and what should be a year of economic revival risks becoming yet another of economic misery and missed opportunities.

The US Federal Reserve benchmark interest rate is currently 3.75 per cent. I expect that to fall to three per cent this year, propelled downwards by a new Fed chairman more likely to do 

Trump’s bidding when it comes to cheap money.
The UK benchmark rate is also 3.75 per cent. Lower inflation will allow us to follow in the Fed’s footsteps towards three per cent. The Eurozone benchmark rate is already two per cent. That probably won’t change. But if it does, it will be down, not up.

Falling inflation followed by more cuts in interest rates are another reason to be cautiously cheerful about the economy in 2026. There’s one more – rearmament, another potential stimulus to the economy.

The Germans are leading the way in Europe with a massive boost to defence spending from a low base. The Poles and Scandinavians are also doing their bit to deter a revanchist Russia from further military adventures with stronger defences.

But Britain is a laggard. Our government talks a lot about extra defence spending but seems to have mislaid its cheque book.

We will spend very little more on rearming in 2026 than we did in 2025 – yet another failure of the Starmer-Reeves government. The military and economic case for a major boost to defence spending is overwhelming. The UK government needs to get on with it.

Falling energy prices. Lower inflation. Falling mortgage rates. More defence spending. Together they amount to a real opportunity to break out of the economic doldrums. What could possibly go wrong? Easy: Starmer-Reeves.

In the summer of 2024 they inherited the fastest-growing economy in the G7. For a while the new government was carried along by that momentum. But the wrecking ball of its first Budget in November 2024 took its toll in 2025.
Growth went from a respectable 0.7 per cent in the first quarter of last year to a worrying 0.3 per cent in the second, a pathetic 0.1 per cent in the third – and a likely stagnant 0.0 per cent in the fourth quarter just ended.

But the sad catalogue of Starmer-Reeves failures doesn’t stop with a slump in growth. It includes higher inflation, rising unemployment (4.4 per cent a year ago, now over 5 per cent), the lowest investment of any G7 economy and reckless borrowing.

The Tories borrowed an incredible £311billion in 2020-21 to counter the impact of the pandemic. Labour wanted them to borrow even more. But within a year the Tories were getting a post-pandemic grip on the public finances: borrowing fell to £120billion in 2021-22.

Labour promptly reversed that: borrowing soared back to £153billion in 2024-25 and looks like being roughly the same in the current financial year.

So, even with some good economic news coming round the corner, what is to stop Starmer-Reeves screwing it up all over again in 2026? Especially since, to save their skins, they are now in thrall to Labour’s soft Left, which has become the dominant force in the party and which wants to borrow, spend and tax more.
Of course, neither might be around for long enough to make a second hash of things.

I have covered the troubles of many previous prime ministers as their party fell out of love with them – from Ted Heath way back in the early 1970s to Margaret Thatcher in the late 1980s, John Major in the 1990s and Tony Blair and Gordon Brown in the first decade of this century. But I have never witnessed anything like the visceral dislike – bordering on hatred – that Labour backbenchers have for Starmer (and, by extension, Reeves).

The settled Labour consensus is that he’s a dud – as useless at politics as he is at policy, twin defects that were amply on display this week after he welcomed an Egyptian activist to our shores, seemingly unaware he was an anti-Semitic, anti-British, anti-white extremist with a violent streak. That had even the PM’s cabinet ministers shaking their heads in despair.

Labour MPs have been biding their time waiting to ditch Starmer after the May elections, which are universally expected to be a disaster for him in England (at least in those parts where Labour is allowing elections), Scotland and Wales. But a growing number are no longer prepared to wait that long: they want to dump him as soon as possible.

This is not necessarily good news for the economy. The bond markets, where governments go to borrow, fear any change at the top would result in an even more Left-wing government. 

They’re right: all potential successors are to Starmer’s Left, bar Health Secretary Wes Streeting – and even he’s tilting that way to curry favour with the soft Left. Manchester Mayor Andy Burham, who doesn’t hide his leadership ambitions, complains about Labour being ‘in hock’ to the bond markets: there’s a simple way to avoid that, Andy — stop borrowing so much from them!

An Angela Rayner government (perish the thought) is hardly likely to be a pinnacle of fiscal rectitude. Ditto one led by Ed Miliband (another perishing thought).

The above three and several more, spent much of 2025 on manoeuvres to replace Starmer. They will pick up where they left off in the New Year, with renewed vigour. The danger for the UK economy is that, in response to these Labour Party machinations indicating a clear lean to the Left, the bond markets decide to dump British debt, forcing up government borrowing costs to unaffordable levels.

That would be the modern equivalent of the 1976 economic crisis under a previous Labour government, which led to the humiliation of being bailed out by the International Monetary Fund. But history doesn’t quite repeat itself.
Rather than a second IMF bailout, the British government would more likely be left to retrench on its own, forced to slash spending and raise taxes because it had run out of room to borrow any more. It would make the so-called austerity of the Cameron-Osborne years look like the good times and split Labour asunder.

I do not predict such a cataclysm for 2026 (though I wouldn’t entirely rule it out either). But if anything is likely to provoke the notorious bond vigilantes to do their worst this year it is the prospect of an even more profligate Labour government than the Starmer-Reeves regime.
It would certainly overwhelm all the potential good economic news that awaits us this year – and it speaks volumes for our current predicament that the best international investors can see for us is a continuation of Starmer-Reeves. Truly blessed we are not.

Compared with Starmer’s ‘end of days’, Kemi Badenoch starts 2026 in much better shape than she began last year. The Tory leader has gained in confidence, come across as the decent person she is and often bested a flat-footed Starmer at Prime Minister’s Questions.
Her (perhaps insurmountable) problem is that she heads a political brand which could be tarnished beyond rescue and which has haemorrhaged support to Reform, which might not be reclaimable.

That said, Reform ended 2025 slipping a little in the polls having peaked at just over 30 per cent (while the Tories started to gain a few points from a very low base) and with a sense in some quarters that Nigel Farage had somewhat lost his mojo. He and his party certainly no longer dominate the national discourse the way they did for much of last year.

We will find out soon enough in 2026 if the Tory revival is real or if Reform quickly bounds back to establish its credentials as the new and dominant party of the Right. Only one or the other can happen – not both. For Starmer there are no good prospects. Even if he survives until the May elections the results will be dismal for him.

Labour will lose control of the Welsh Parliament, which it has run since the latter was established in 1998. A year ago Labour was poised to take the Scottish Parliament. Now, thanks to Starmer’s deep unpopularity north of the border, the SNP will hold on to power and Labour could come third (behind the SNP and even Reform).
While Reform could be given a new lease of life with a strong showing in England’s local elections in May, Labour will continue to shed its Left base to the Greens and their glib new leader.

I started off with some good cheer for the New Year. My fear is good economic prospects will be more than thwarted by bad politics. Starmer and Reeves will be brought down by their own socialist conceit: that economic growth can be fostered by a bigger public sector, higher taxes, more public spending.

It can’t. In fact, that’s how you stifle growth. But, amazingly, as both are dispatched to the wilderness for failing, Labour will double down on its socialist fantasies –and what should be a year of economic revival risks becoming yet another of economic misery and missed opportunities.

My son didn’t invite me to his wedding, he just texted, “I’m sorry, Mom, it’s a fancy event and my fiancée doesn’t want you there, she thinks you’re a bit too dramatic.” I calmly replied, “That’s okay, just enjoy your day,” then quietly did one thing on my own. Two hours later, my phone was buzzing nonstop with 22 missed calls. My name is Margaret Lewis, I’m 68 years old, and I live in a small brick house on the east side of Columbus, Ohio. That text came in on a Tuesday afternoon while I was standing at my kitchen sink, rinsing out a coffee mug with “Best Mom” faded on the side, the one he painted for me in second grade. Outside, you could hear an old pickup rolling past and a neighbor’s TV playing some baseball game. Inside, it was just me, the humming fridge, and a message that turned my whole world sideways. I read it three times, every word hitting a little harder than the last. “Fancy event.” “Doesn’t want you there.” “Too dramatic.” For a moment, I thought my hands would start shaking, or that I’d do what he and his fiancée clearly expected—burst into tears, plead, make a scene, prove them right. Instead, I wiped my hands on a dish towel, sat down at my little Formica table, and stared out the window at the American flag swinging lazily on my neighbor’s porch. I didn’t argue. I didn’t ask who had been talking about me behind closed doors, or how we got from “you’re my hero, Mom” to “you’re not invited.” I just typed, “That’s okay, just enjoy your day,” added a little heart, and hit send. Somewhere across town, in whatever trendy venue they’d picked with hanging lights and champagne walls, I’m sure that text made everything easier. No fight. No guilt. Just the quiet older woman who knew her place.
But here’s what nobody at that “fancy event” knew: I have spent my entire adult life making things work in this country when they absolutely should have fallen apart. Double shifts at the diner off I-70, late nights scrubbing offices in downtown Columbus while the skyline glowed, clipping coupons at this same table so my kids could have new shoes when mine had holes in them. I buried my husband, kept a roof over our heads, and helped my son through college from this house. Now I was being told I was a liability to the aesthetic.
So I took a breath, reached for the drawer where I keep the things that really matter, and decided if they wanted distance from me, I would finally give them exactly what they were asking for.
Before I tell you what I did after that text—what I changed in less than one afternoon that turned their perfect day into 22 missed calls on my screen—I want to know something from you. Where are you watching from right now? Are you in New York, Dallas, Seattle, maybe somewhere outside the U.S. with my little Midwest story playing through your headphones while you cook dinner or try to fall asleep? My son didn’t invite me to his wedding, he just texted, “I’m sorry, Mom, it’s a fancy event and my fiancée doesn’t want you there, she thinks you’re a bit too dramatic.” I calmly replied, “That’s okay, just enjoy your day,” then quietly did one thing on my own. Two hours later, my phone was buzzing nonstop with 22 missed calls. My name is Margaret Lewis, I’m 68 years old, and I live in a small brick house on the east side of Columbus, Ohio. That text came in on a Tuesday afternoon while I was standing at my kitchen sink, rinsing out a coffee mug with “Best Mom” faded on the side, the one he painted for me in second grade. Outside, you could hear an old pickup rolling past and a neighbor’s TV playing some baseball game. Inside, it was just me, the humming fridge, and a message that turned my whole world sideways. I read it three times, every word hitting a little harder than the last. “Fancy event.” “Doesn’t want you there.” “Too dramatic.” For a moment, I thought my hands would start shaking, or that I’d do what he and his fiancée clearly expected—burst into tears, plead, make a scene, prove them right. Instead, I wiped my hands on a dish towel, sat down at my little Formica table, and stared out the window at the American flag swinging lazily on my neighbor’s porch. I didn’t argue. I didn’t ask who had been talking about me behind closed doors, or how we got from “you’re my hero, Mom” to “you’re not invited.” I just typed, “That’s okay, just enjoy your day,” added a little heart, and hit send. Somewhere across town, in whatever trendy venue they’d picked with hanging lights and champagne walls, I’m sure that text made everything easier. No fight. No guilt. Just the quiet older woman who knew her place.
But here’s what nobody at that “fancy event” knew: I have spent my entire adult life making things work in this country when they absolutely should have fallen apart. Double shifts at the diner off I-70, late nights scrubbing offices in downtown Columbus while the skyline glowed, clipping coupons at this same table so my kids could have new shoes when mine had holes in them. I buried my husband, kept a roof over our heads, and helped my son through college from this house. Now I was being told I was a liability to the aesthetic.
So I took a breath, reached for the drawer where I keep the things that really matter, and decided if they wanted distance from me, I would finally give them exactly what they were asking for.
Before I tell you what I did after that text—what I changed in less than one afternoon that turned their perfect day into 22 missed calls on my screen—I want to know something from you. Where are you watching from right now? Are you in New York, Dallas, Seattle, maybe somewhere outside the U.S. with my little Midwest story playing through your headphones while you cook dinner or try to fall asleep? Because when a son decides his mother is too “dramatic” for his big day, he forgets one thing: the quiet move she makes afterward can change everything.— 🚀✨The of to a and in that is for on it with as My son didn’t invite me to his wedding, he just texted, “I’m sorry, Mom, it’s a fancy event and my fiancée doesn’t want you there, she thinks you’re a bit too dramatic.” I calmly replied, “That’s okay, just enjoy your day,” then quietly did one thing on my own. Two hours later, my phone was buzzing nonstop with 22 missed calls. My name is Margaret Lewis, I’m 68 years old, and I live in a small brick house on the east side of Columbus, Ohio. That text came in on a Tuesday afternoon while I was standing at my kitchen sink, rinsing out a coffee mug with “Best Mom” faded on the side, the one he painted for me in second grade. Outside, you could hear an old pickup rolling past and a neighbor’s TV playing some baseball game. Inside, it was just me, the humming fridge, and a message that turned my whole world sideways. I read it three times, every word hitting a little harder than the last. “Fancy event.” “Doesn’t want you there.” “Too dramatic.” For a moment, I thought my hands would start shaking, or that I’d do what he and his fiancée clearly expected—burst into tears, plead, make a scene, prove them right. Instead, I wiped my hands on a dish towel, sat down at my little Formica table, and stared out the window at the American flag swinging lazily on my neighbor’s porch. I didn’t argue. I didn’t ask who had been talking about me behind closed doors, or how we got from “you’re my hero, Mom” to “you’re not invited.” I just typed, “That’s okay, just enjoy your day,” added a little heart, and hit send. Somewhere across town, in whatever trendy venue they’d picked with hanging lights and champagne walls, I’m sure that text made everything easier. No fight. No guilt. Just the quiet older woman who knew her place.
But here’s what nobody at that “fancy event” knew: I have spent my entire adult life making things work in this country when they absolutely should have fallen apart. Double shifts at the diner off I-70, late nights scrubbing offices in downtown Columbus while the skyline glowed, clipping coupons at this same table so my kids could have new shoes when mine had holes in them. I buried my husband, kept a roof over our heads, and helped my son through college from this house. Now I was being told I was a liability to the aesthetic.
So I took a breath, reached for the drawer where I keep the things that really matter, and decided if they wanted distance from me, I would finally give them exactly what they were asking for.
Before I tell you what I did after that text—what I changed in less than one afternoon that turned their perfect day into 22 missed calls on my screen—I want to know something from you. Where are you watching from right now? Are you in New York, Dallas, Seattle, maybe somewhere outside the U.S. with my little Midwest story playing through your headphones while you cook dinner or try to fall asleep? Because when a son decides his mother is too “dramatic” for his big day, he forgets one thing: the quiet move she makes afterward can change everything.— 🚀✨The of to a and in that is for on it with as caption:
Monday, February 16, 2026

The Storm Prediction Center has issued a Marginal Risk (Level 1/5) for much of the central and southern California coastal counties today.

This is a cold-core, high-shear setup with a strong Pacific system moving inland.

⏰ TIMING

• Central Coast: Around 10 AM – 2 PM PST
• Southern CA (LA Basin southward): Noon – 4 PM PST
• Northern CA / SW Oregon (Late Night): After Midnight

🌬️ PRIMARY THREAT

• Strong wind gusts (50+ mph possible)
• Brief, shallow tornado spin-ups cannot be ruled out
• Small hail or graupel possible

📍 WHAT’S HAPPENING

A potent upper trough is moving across California today with:

• 100+ kt mid-level jet
• Strengthening surface low over central CA
• Cold front sweeping down the coastline after 18Z

Strong wind convergence along the front will create a narrow line of convection. Embedded thunderstorms are possible within that line.

Instability is limited, and cool surface temperatures will keep the tornado threat low — but not zero.

These would be brief, quick spin-ups if they occur.

🌧️ INTERIOR VALLEYS

Heavy cloud cover and precipitation will limit daytime heating.
Very little surface-based instability is expected inland.

The stronger thunderstorm potential stays closer to the coast.

🌨️ LATE TONIGHT – NORTHERN CA / SW OREGON

A secondary upper trough drops south overnight with very cold air aloft (near -35°C at 500mb).

This may produce:

• Low-topped convection
• Graupel showers
• Locally strong wind gusts

Surface temps will be in the 40s.

🌡️ Temperature Outlook (NDFD Guidance)

Highs Today:
• 50s to low 60s Coastal CA
• 40s Northern CA
• 60s Desert Areas
• 70s Southern Arizona

Cool, unstable air mass in place behind the front.

We are NOT chasing today.
We are monitoring and will post updates if needed.

If you’re along the central or southern California coast today, be prepared for sudden strong wind gusts with passing storms.

caption:
🛡️ Tech Magic or Trap? Your Bank Secrets SAFE—Fools the Fakers, Sparks the Seekers!

🛡️Friends, tech races ahead—UPI zaps money in seconds, Aadhaar unlocks dreams. But that chill when a "bank call" asks your OTP? Or spam promising "free cash"? You're not alone. Here's the gentle truth: Your data is LOCKED tighter than you think, and fraudsters are just smoke. No tech edge beats inner wisdom. Read on—let it light your path, blind their tricks. 

Myth Busted: 

Who's Peeking at YOUR Bank/Aadhaar?ZERO outsiders own your details!UIDAI/Aadhaar: Holds ONLY name, address, biometrics (encrypted FOREVER). NO bank info, PAN, health, property—ever! Banks send OTP/biometrics for check; UIDAI says "yes/no," NOTHING else. Aadhaar alone? Useless like card number sans PIN. 

Banks: 
YOUR account visible ONLY to YOU + bank staff (RBI audited). UPI? Tokenized—fraud sees "****1234," not full deets. Govt/Schemes: PM-KISAN, PMAY use consent-based auth—data siloed, DPDPA fines ₹250 Cr for leaks. No shadowy cabal. Laws shield like a mother's embrace.Fraud's Smoke: Why They Fail, How You ShineThey hunt fear— "Account hacked! Share OTP!" But truth disarms:"Urgent Call?" Banks NEVER ask OTP/PIN/CVV. Hang up, dial official number. 

Phony Apps/Links? Official stores only. Alerts ON for every ₹1 tx. SIM/Loan Tricks? e-KYC needs YOUR live biometrics—can't fake live eyes/finger. Daily Shields (Effortless Nobility):Strong Locks: Unique PINs (no 1234), 2FA everywhere.

Watchful Eye: App alerts + monthly statements—spot odd, freeze instant.Verify First: Call back via app/site. Doubt? RBI 1930 helpline FREE.Limits Rule: UPI cap ₹5k first-time; card limits daily.Result? 62% fraud drop via biometrics. You're the fortress they can't breach. 

The Subtle Spark: 
Inner Power Over Outer TechTech evolves, but fraud preys eternal greed/fear. 

Pause: 

Is this "help" or hook? Nobility whispers—protect self quietly, share wisdom kindly. Report scams (cybercrime.gov.in)—save neighbors without fanfare.You're not vulnerable; you're vigilant. Frauds chase shadows; you walk in light. Share this ripple—good hearts catch it, dark ones miss the glow.

#DataSafe #FraudProof #InnerWisdom #TechSmartTN

caption:
Twelve races went postward on Sunday (Feb. 15) at Saratoga with a lofty handle at $803,695.79.

With a tight finish in the $16,500 Fillies and Mares Winners Over / Open Handicap Pace, Island Bouhinia A and Jacob Cutting came out on top, winning by a head in 1:55. Amanda Kelley trains the seven-year-old daughter of Betting Line and the Sportswriter mare Island Five Star for owners Sartin Racing LLC and S&K Misfit Racing LLC. Island Bouhinia pushed her career earnings to $113,912 with the win.

Waitforever N (Leon Bailey) was second with Perfect Queen (Matty Athearn) third.

Drivers Larry Stalbaum and Jacob Cutting each had doubles on the card. Stalbaum was the only double winning trainer. 

Jumping Jake, trained by Tony Ciuffetelli and driven by Brett Beckwith, won by the greatest margin of victory with a 6-1/4 length triumph.

Swedish Starlet N, driven by Matty Athearn for trainer Jimmy Nickerson and owners Tim Bojarski and Anthony Gruppo, posted the fastest time on the card with a 1:54.4 win. 

Off at 12-1, Forgot Thewallet A was the greatest upset winner on Sunday, returning $25.78 to win in line to Jay Randall for trainer Rob Harmon.

Divided We Fall, Celcius, and Forgot Thewallet A were each repeat winners from the previous week of racing at Saratoga.

Racing at Saratoga resumes on Monday (Feb. 16) with 11 races starting at 12 p.m. The $16,500 Winners Over / Open Handicap Trot tops the mixed card with eight trotters lining up behind the gate. The 5-2 morning line favorite is Ordained and driver/trainer Larry Stalbaum in post five. Memorynimagination (Matty Athearn) is picked second from post six and Platinum As (Brett Beckwith) is picked third from the eight hole.

#SaratogaHarness2026

PM કિસાન સન્માન નિધિ યોજનાના ખેડૂત લાભાર્થીઓ માટે મહત્ત્વના સમાચાર આવ્યા છે. પીએમ કિસાન સન્માન નિધિ યોજનાના 16માં હપ્તા માટે E-KYC ફરજીયાત કરાયું છે. ગુજરાતમાં 21 ફેબ્રુઆરી સુધી KYC ઝુંબેશ ચાલશે. ગ્રામ સેવક, તાલુકા વિકાસ અધિકારી તથા જિલ્લા કક્ષાએ જિલ્લા કૃષિ અધિકારીની કચેરીમાં ફેસ ઓથેન્ટિકેશન દ્વારા E-KYC કરાવી શકાશે. મોબાઈલ એપ્લિકેશન દ્વારા પણ ખેડૂતો E-KYC કરી શકશે.

#kisansammannidhiyojana #KYC #E-KYC #AgriculturalOfficer #gscard #gujaratsamachar

JP Nadda said Mamata Didi has done injustice to farmers in West Bengal

JP Nadda on Saturday Slamming the West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee over not implementing Prime Minister's Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana in the state

"Mamata Didi has done injustice to the farmers here. She in her stubbornness, ego and pride, did not roll out PM's Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana in West Bengal. 
 This has kept over 70 lakh farmers deprived of its benefit,” Nadda said while addressing in Malda. The BJP chief said that Mamata announced that she will also roll out the scheme in the state after when around 25 lakh people urged to the Centre for the matter and the elections were around the corner in the state.

“When around 25 lakh people urged to the Centre, then Mamata Ji said I will also implement Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana. Mamata Ji, elections are around the corner, what is the point repenting when the damage has already been done?” Nadda accused.

देश के करोड़ों किसानों के लिए बड़ी खबर है! केंद्र सरकार प्रधानमंत्री किसान सम्मान निधि योजना (PM-Kisan) की 20वीं किस्त जारी करने जा रही है। 2 अगस्त को सुबह 11 बजे, पीएम मोदी 9.7 करोड़ से अधिक किसानों के बैंक खातों में ₹2,000 ट्रांसफर करेंगे।

कैसे चेक करें अपना नाम?
अगर आप जानना चाहते हैं कि आपको इस किस्त का लाभ मिलेगा या नहीं, तो आप इन स्टेप्स को फॉलो कर सकते हैं:

आधिकारिक वेबसाइट: सबसे पहले pmkisan.gov.in पर जाएं।

"Farmer Corner" में जाकर "Beneficiary Status" पर क्लिक करें।

अपना राज्य, जिला, ब्लॉक और गांव चुनकर लिस्ट में अपना नाम देख लें।

यह योजना फरवरी 2019 में शुरू की गई थी, जिसके तहत पात्र किसानों को हर साल ₹6,000 की आर्थिक मदद दी जाती है।

ಪಿಎಂ ಕಿಸಾನ್‌ ಸಮ್ಮಾನ್‌ ನಿಧಿ ಯೋಜನೆಯಡಿ 20ನೇ ಕಂತಿನ ಹಣ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಅಂಗವಾಗಿ ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಗ್ರಾಮಾಂತರ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆ ದೊಡ್ಡಬಳ್ಳಾಪುರ ತಾಲೂಕಿನ ಹಾಡೋನಹಳ್ಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕೃಷಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ ಕೇಂದ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಜರುಗಿದ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾಲ್ಗೊಳ್ಳಲಾಯಿತು. 

ಪ್ರಧಾನಿ ಶ್ರೀ @narendramodi ಅವರು ಇಂದು 'ಕಿಸಾನ್ ಸಮ್ಮಾನ್ ನಿಧಿ' ಯೋಜನೆಯ 20ನೇ ಕಂತಿನ ಹಣವನ್ನು ವಾರಾಣಸಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಂಕೇತಿಕವಾಗಿ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದು ದೇಶಾದ್ಯಂತ ಸುಮಾರು 9 ಕೋಟಿ 70 ಲಕ್ಷಕ್ಕಿಂತಲೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ರೈತ ಫಲಾನುಭವಿ ರೈತರ ಖಾತೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಒಟ್ಟು 20,500 ಕೋಟಿ ರೂಪಾಯಿ ಹಣ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಜಮಾವಣೆಯಾಗಲಿದೆ.

ಈ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ರೈಲ್ವೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಜಲಶಕ್ತಿ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಸಚಿವರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ @VSOMANNA_BJP, ರಾಜ್ಯದ ಆಹಾರ, ನಾಗರಿಕ ಸರಬರಾಜು ಮತ್ತು ಗ್ರಾಹಕ ವ್ಯವಹಾರಗಳ ಇಲಾಖೆ ಸಚಿವರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ @KHMuniyappaklr, ದೊಡ್ಡಬಳ್ಳಾಪುರದ ಶಾಸಕರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ @dheerajmuniraj, ಜಿಲ್ಲಾಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳಾದ ಶ್ರೀ ಬಸವರಾಜು, ಕೃಷಿ ವಿವಿ ಉಪಕುಲಪತಿಗಳಾದ ಡಾ.ಎಸ್.ವಿ.ಸುರೇಶ್, ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ಅನೇಕ ಗಣ್ಯರು, ರೈತ ಬಾಂಧವರು ಹಾಗೂ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕರು ಉಪಸ್ಥಿತರಿದ್ದರು.

ಪಿಎಂ ಕಿಸಾನ್‌ ಸಮ್ಮಾನ್‌ ನಿಧಿ ಯೋಜನೆಯಡಿ 20ನೇ ಕಂತಿನ ಹಣ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಅಂಗವಾಗಿ ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಗ್ರಾಮಾಂತರ ಜಿಲ್ಲೆ ದೊಡ್ಡಬಳ್ಳಾಪುರ ತಾಲೂಕಿನ ಹಾಡೋನಹಳ್ಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಕೃಷಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ ಕೇಂದ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಜರುಗಿದ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾಲ್ಗೊಳ್ಳಲಾಯಿತು. 

ಪ್ರಧಾನಿ ಶ್ರೀ @narendramodi ಅವರು ಇಂದು 'ಕಿಸಾನ್ ಸಮ್ಮಾನ್ ನಿಧಿ' ಯೋಜನೆಯ 20ನೇ ಕಂತಿನ ಹಣವನ್ನು ವಾರಾಣಸಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಂಕೇತಿಕವಾಗಿ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದು ದೇಶಾದ್ಯಂತ ಸುಮಾರು 9 ಕೋಟಿ 70 ಲಕ್ಷಕ್ಕಿಂತಲೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ರೈತ ಫಲಾನುಭವಿ ರೈತರ ಖಾತೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಒಟ್ಟು 20,500 ಕೋಟಿ ರೂಪಾಯಿ ಹಣ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಜಮಾವಣೆಯಾಗಲಿದೆ.

ಈ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ರೈಲ್ವೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಜಲಶಕ್ತಿ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಸಚಿವರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ @VSOMANNA_BJP, ರಾಜ್ಯದ ಆಹಾರ, ನಾಗರಿಕ ಸರಬರಾಜು ಮತ್ತು ಗ್ರಾಹಕ ವ್ಯವಹಾರಗಳ ಇಲಾಖೆ ಸಚಿವರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ @KHMuniyappaklr, ದೊಡ್ಡಬಳ್ಳಾಪುರದ ಶಾಸಕರಾದ ಶ್ರೀ @dheerajmuniraj, ಜಿಲ್ಲಾಧಿಕಾರಿಗಳಾದ ಶ್ರೀ ಬಸವರಾಜು, ಕೃಷಿ ವಿವಿ ಉಪಕುಲಪತಿಗಳಾದ ಡಾ.ಎಸ್.ವಿ.ಸುರೇಶ್, ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ಅನೇಕ ಗಣ್ಯರು, ರೈತ ಬಾಂಧವರು ಹಾಗೂ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕರು ಉಪಸ್ಥಿತರಿದ್ದರು.

caption:
आयुष्मान भारत कार्ड, जिसे PM-JAY (प्रधानमंत्री जन आरोग्य योजना) के नाम से भी जाना जाता है, भारत सरकार द्वारा 2018 में शुरू की गई एक क्रांतिकारी स्वास्थ्य बीमा योजना है। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य देश के आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर परिवारों को गंभीर बीमारियों के इलाज के लिए वित्तीय सुरक्षा कवच प्रदान करना है।

इस योजना के तहत, पात्र परिवार को प्रति वर्ष ₹5 लाख तक का कैशलेस स्वास्थ्य कवर मिलता है, जिसका लाभ परिवार के सभी सदस्य मिलकर उठा सकते हैं। सबसे बड़ा फायदा यह है कि इस राशि का इस्तेमाल साल भर में असीमित बार किया जा सकता है, बशर्ते कुल खर्च ₹5 लाख की सीमा के अंदर हो। यह लाभ देश भर के हजारों मान्यता प्राप्त सरकारी और प्राइवेट अस्पतालों में पोर्टेबल है, यानी आप किसी भी राज्य में इलाज करवा सकते हैं।

यह कार्ड मुख्य रूप से बड़े इलाज और सर्जरी जैसे हार्ट ऑपरेशन, कैंसर उपचार, अंग प्रत्यारोपण और न्यूरो सर्जरी आदि के लिए है। हालाँकि, सामान्य OPD परामर्श या छोटे-मोटे टेस्ट इसके दायरे में नहीं आते। कार्ड बनवाने की पूरी प्रक्रिया डिजिटल और निःशुल्क है, जिसे आधार आधारित आयुष्मान ऐप के माध्यम से आसानी से पूरा किया जा सकता है।

संक्षेप में, आयुष्मान कार्ड गरीबी रेखा से नीचे जीवनयापन करने वाले करोड़ों भारतीयों के लिए एक वरदान है, जो उन्हें गंभीर स्वास्थ्य संकट के समय भारी आर्थिक ऋण से बचाता है और गुणवत्तापूर्ण इलाज की गारंटी देता है।

caption:
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, while presenting the Union Budget, said that the country is expected to grow at 9.27 per cent in the coming year. With a focus on four pillars of development — inclusive development, productivity enhancement, energy transition and climate action — the Budget gives a blueprint of economy from India at 75 to India at 100, Sitharaman said.

• In a significant move that is believed to have brought cryptocurrencies and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) under a tax net, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday announced a 30% 'crypto tax' on the proceeds made on the transfer of virtual digital assets.

• A new digital rupee powered by blockchain technology will also be issued by the Reserve Bank of India starting 2022-23.

• Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that the government will roll out 5G telecom services during the financial year 2022-2023. She  also said that the spectrum auction for the same will also be conducted in FY 22-23.

• The FM said that the government’s massive procurement of wheat in Rabi season 2021-22 and the estimated procurement of paddy in Kharif season 2021-22 will give cover 1208 lakh metric tonnes of wheat & paddy from 163 lakh farmers.

She said Rs 2.37 lakh crores will be the humungous amount of direct payment of MSP value to their accounts.

• Meanwhile, the finance minister also noted that 80 lakh affordable houses will be completed at Rs 44,000 cr under PM Awas Yojna in 2022-23. 

• Meanwhile, Sitharaman also announced the extension of the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) till March 2023, in what could be a big boost for the country’s Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).

More to follow.

caption:
The country's second Light House Project (LHP) in Rajkot is marred by complaints of corruption and substandard construction.

Constructed under the PM Awas Yojna, the project was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself two years ago.

The first LHP is located in Chennai.

Built at a staggering cost of Rs 118 crores, the Rajkot project comprises 1,144 flats, touted to be constructed using advanced German technology. However, instead of fulfilling its promise, the only such project in Gujarat has left locals grappling with persistent issues like moisture, cracks, crumbling walls, and overflowing drains.

Despite repeated appeals to the administration, no action has been taken, prompting residents to threaten protests to demand accountability.

The Light House Project in Rajkot comprises 1,144 houses across 11 towers of 13 floors, each tower spread over 6,741.66 sq.m. With eight flats per floor. Each house costs Rs 10.39 lakh, funded by Rs 5.50 lakh from the Central Government, Rs 1.50 lakh from the State Government, and Rs 3.39 lakh paid by beneficiaries.

The flats were handed over to the deserving people two years ago by the Prime Minister himself.

Link in bio.

caption:
I was wearing a shirt yesterday that said PMA, the phrase popularized by Washington Hardcore legends The Bad Brains and bought into my life by the big homies @xlgh1157x and @tobymorse....anyway I was watching my step-son doodle away and he busted this out un-prompted..how cute is his awesome phonetic attempt at spelling! 

He was mortified he got it wrong and rushed to correct it. Anyways, he chucked all the ✖️✖️✖️s around it, and it made me pause and reflect just how much our little ones are sponges. 

I generally wear ideas and feelings on my shirts, and now he can read, I’m mindful that the energy in the messages are super important for his development as much as for my own vibe. 

That’s not to deny my (our human) moments of melancholic sadness and at times poor mental health, but I wanna be mindful about romanticizing them, lest little man gets the wrong idea. 

Conversely, I was stoked to be able to explain to him at 6 years old about PMA, and the straightedge XXXs, what they mean and why I have them tattooed. 

It made pause and really reminded me how what we put into the world is shaping others, whether it’s our children, our friends or complete strangers. We are continuing negative narratives or contributing to positive ones every action, every word, every t shirt, every post, so maybe we all need to pay attention to what side we are making deposits into it.

#PMA #StraightEdge #RaisingKids #Atechud

caption:
“At first they’ll ask you why you’re doing it. But later they’ll ask you, how you did it!” ⁣
⁣
One of my favorite quotes when I was a waitress/student and just started my home wellness biz 10 years ago! I wanted to make that quote come true for myself. ⁣
⁣
I remember a time when people absolutely believed I lived in a dingy apartment with a mattress on the floor. It was no surprise! 🙃⁣
⁣
I had to slowly find my footing as a young adult and was totally lost in my self destructive behavior before I got sober.⁣
⁣
Honestly, I got a SLOW start to adulthood and was “behind” my peers in life but your girl made up for it with hard ass work, humility and vulnerability!⁣
⁣
When I started this business people absolutely thought I was crazy! They only knew me from before and you better believe they were vocal about it and wanted me to stay there. ⁣
⁣
If I had every negative, disheartening, unsupportive comment or email I’d have an entire book to show you but instead I prefer to show you what can happen when you stop letting those comments stop you.⁣
⁣
It always makes me smile when I get comments like this because I too, can’t believe this is real most days. ⁣
⁣
I’m writing this laying on my bed with views of the mountain range over the water vs renting a room in some dudes house to throw my mattress down in and I just WISH more people would realize their potential. ⁣
⁣
If there is any ounce of you that believes your life has more potential then PLEASE do me a favor and pursue it! YOU CAN DO HARD THINGS BABE!⁣
⁣
If you don’t know where to start, I can always help you! That’s my job. Paying this opportunity forward to people who want to live a life that some people will say isn’t real. ⁣
⁣
The quote should be changed to “At first they’ll ask you why you’re doing it. But later they’ll say it’s not real.” < that’s goals right there!⁣
⁣
All jokes aside, this ISN’T ABOUT THEM. This is about YOUR LIFE. Social media isn’t real! The REAL life is what you live when you’re off social media. Learn to monetize your scroll & live a life you will remember.

👥🥋 At Premier Martial Arts, we're more than just a team - we're one big family! 💪❤️

Free things to do in Chongqing

Drone Show : Every Saturday at 8:30 PM, the sky comes alive with hundreds of drones painting the skyline. It’s futuristic, magical, and totally Instagram-worthy

Liziba :Only in Chongqing: a metro train glides straight through a building like it’s the most normal thing ever. Iconic and mind-blowing at the same time

Deyi World : Neon lights, loud energy, and endless vibes. Deyi World is where Chongqing nightlife hits different

Kuinxing Building : It looks like a regular ground floor… until you realize you’re actually on the 22nd floor! Total mind-bender and photo gold

The Ring Mall: Futuristic design meets a suspended tropical jungle with waterfalls. A shopping trip that feels like stepping into the future

Hongya Cave from Qiansimen Bridge: Neon reflections on the river, a cinematic cityscape, and the heartbeat of Chongqing at night

Shibati : Old Chongqing charm stacked on steep stairways, glowing lanterns, and hidden cafés. Perfect for wandering and getting lost in time

Xiahaoli : Winding stairways, vintage vibes, endless cafés, and boutique shops. The charm of old Chongqing condensed into one area

Watch the Yangtze Cable Car : Glide over the river and take in the city from a whole new angle. Suspended views that are pure magic

caption:
-SHADOWSCENT-
.
« Lorsque que vous craignez de perdre une chose, vous saisissez toutes les occasions de la savourer. »
.
Hello booksta !
.
C’EST LHEURE DU GOÛTER ! 
.
Oulalalala c’était les montagnes russes cette lecture...Un coup c’etait très lent et un coup c’était  dynamique. L’histoire était originale avec du potentiel mais pas assez exploité à mon goût.
.
Tout d’abord j’adore l’univers du parfum, avec ce roman j’ai été servi, ensuite j’adore quand y a 2 points de vues et j’ai largement préféré celui de Ash que je trouve plus touchant. Et puis la fin qui a sauvé la lenteur du récit.
Euuuh la couverture est belle aussi (oui je fais genre je gonfle les points positifs)
.
Ce que j’ai moins aimé : ce soit disant triangle amoureux 🙄, la simplicité de certaines missions et la fin (attend mais tu viens de dire que tu l’as aimé) je m’explique : c’est trop flou, j’ai trop de questions.
.
Vais-je lire la suite ? Mmmmmm oui mais ça dépend de beaucoup de chose, si j’ai rien à lire de ouf, si on me dit que la suite est trop bien, si on me le donne gratuitement lol enfin bon je rigole mais c’est à réfléchir quand même finalement je me rends compte que j’ai grave un avis mitigé.
.
Tu vas manger quoi pour le goûter ? Oui ça m’intéresse 😂
.
Sinon tu as lu ce bouquin ? Il te tente ?
.
#shadowscent #pmfreestone #leparfumdelombre #bookstagram #picsart #bookstagrammer #bookstagramfrance #thedarkestbloom #lecture #curentlyreading #tbr #bookstagrameuse #book

Das erste Verlagsprogramm umfasst insgesamt 15 Bücher – vom niedlichen Bilderbuch über monstermäßige und ponytastische Kinderbücher bis hin zu atmosphärischen Jugendbüchern bietet DRAGONFLY neben höchst verkäuflichen, populären Titeln und bekannten Autorinnen und Autoren auch neuen und besonderen Geschichten Platz.

・
Wenn ihr die Galerie zur Seite wischt, könnt ihr schon mal einen Blick auf das allererste Verlagsprogramm »HERBST/WINTER 2019/2020« werfen. 
Meine absoluten Favoriten sind natürlich die vier Jugendbuchtitel und das Bilderbuch über das kleine Lesemuffelmädchen, das keine Bücher mag ❤️

caption:
Tata Power Launches Affordable Rooftop Solar Solutions in Odisha.

Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited (TPREL), a subsidiary of Tata Power, has launched its affordable rooftop solar solutions in Bhubaneswar under the 'Ghar Ghar Solar' campaign. With an initial cost starting at just ₹2,499 for a 1 kW system and subsidies covering up to 40%, the initiative aims to drive solar adoption among households. 

Backed by central and state schemes like the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, which offers up to ₹78,000 in subsidies, the campaign targets 3 lakh installations in Odisha and 10 lakh across India over 3-5 years. TPREL is collaborating with OREDA to boost solar penetration and is also introducing lifestyle solar products. 

Tata Power’s stock traded flat at ₹393.50, down 0.63%, with a market cap of ₹1.25 lakh crore. The firm posted a 47% YoY profit jump in renewables and plans to explore export opportunities amid rising domestic demand.

#GharGharSolar #TataPowerGreen #SolarForAll #CleanEnergyOdisha #RooftopRevolution #GoSolarIndia #OREDA #SustainableLiving #PMFreeElectricity #GreenFutureNow #Odisha #Bhubaneswar

caption:
प्रधानमंत्री सूर्य घर मुफ्त बिजली योजना (Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme) के लाभ आमजन तक पहुंचाने और व्यापक जन-जागरूकता के लिए जिला कलेक्टोरेट परिसर से प्रचार रथ को कलेक्टर मयंक चतुर्वेदी ने हरी झंडी दिखाकर रवाना किया। यह प्रचार रथ जिले के शहरी और ग्रामीण अंचलों का भ्रमण कर नागरिकों को योजना की विस्तृत जानकारी देगा तथा उन्हें इससे होने वाले आर्थिक व सामाजिक लाभों से अवगत कराएगा।

कलेक्टर श्री चतुर्वेदी ने कहा कि प्रधानमंत्री सूर्य घर मुफ्त बिजली योजना आम उपभोक्ताओं को ऊर्जा के क्षेत्र में आत्मनिर्भर बनाने का सशक्त माध्यम है। उन्होंने बताया कि योजना के तहत उपभोक्ता अपने मकान की छत पर सौर पैनल स्थापित कर न केवल घरेलू आवश्यकताओं की पूर्ति कर सकते हैं, बल्कि अतिरिक्त बिजली को ग्रिड में बेचकर अतिरिक्त आमदनी भी अर्जित कर सकते हैं।

उन्होंने कहा कि केंद्र एवं राज्य सरकार मिलकर उपभोक्ताओं को आकर्षक सब्सिडी प्रदान कर रही है, जिससे यह योजना आमजन के लिए सरल, किफायती और लाभकारी सिद्ध हो रही है। इस अवसर पर अधीक्षण अभियंता गुंजन शर्मा, कार्यपालन अभियंता रामकुमार राव, नरेंद्र नायक सहित बिजली विभाग के अधिकारी-कर्मचारी और बड़ी संख्या में नागरिक उपस्थित रहे।

प्रधानमंत्री सूर्य घर मुफ्त बिजली योजना के अंतर्गत 1 किलोवाट प्लांट से प्रतिमाह लगभग 120 यूनिट बिजली उत्पादन होता है। इसमें केंद्र सरकार 30 हजार रुपए एवं राज्य सरकार 15 हजार रुपए सब्सिडी प्रदान करती है। 2 किलोवाट प्लांट से प्रतिमाह लगभग 240 यूनिट बिजली उत्पादन होता है।

इसमें केंद्र सरकार 60 हजार रुपए एवं राज्य सरकार 30 हजार रुपए सब्सिडी देती है। 3 किलोवाट प्लांट से प्रतिमाह लगभग 360 यूनिट बिजली उत्पादन होता है। इसमें केंद्र सरकार 78 हजार रुपए एवं राज्य सरकार 30 हजार रुपए सब्सिडी देती है। शेष राशि उपभोक्ता स्वयं वहन करेंगे। जिसे बैंक ऋण सुविधा के माध्यम से भी प्राप्त किया जा सकता है।

caption:
Greater penetration and usage of LPG as a cooking fuel is estimated to have prevented at least 1.5 lakh pollution-related premature deaths in the year 2019 alone, according to the first independent impact assessment of the government’s flagship Ujjwala programme.

The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) also helped in avoiding at least 1.8 million tonnes of PM2.5 emissions that year, this assessment has found.

The study, by Ajay Nagpure, Ritesh Patidar and Vandna Tyagi, who work for the World Resources Institute (WRI) India, is ongoing and still to be peer reviewed. Nagpure, a PhD from IIT Roorkee, has been involved in air pollution-related research for 18 years.

Tyagi, an environmental engineer, was formerly a research fellow at IIT Roorkee, and Patidar, a 2017 graduate from the same institute, has been researching sustainable clean cooking energy solutions, air pollution and related policies.

The researchers maintain that the benefits of Ujjwala measured by them were conservative estimates and the actual benefits could be even higher.

“The avoidance of premature deaths, for example, has been estimated only for indoor air pollution. But cooking fuel also contributes to outdoor air pollution. Earlier studies have indicated that biomass burning in household cooking could be contributing 30-40 per cent of outdoor air pollution. We have not estimated the health or emission benefits of reduction in outdoor air pollution,” Nagpure told The Indian Express.

“Also, the benefits have been estimated for the year 2019 only. Similar benefits would have accrued in subsequent years as well, though we do not have full data as of now. The cumulative benefit of this one single intervention is huge. I would say Ujjwala Yojana would be one of the most effective government interventions to improve air quality and reduce health risks from air pollution,” he said.

For estimating the avoided deaths, Nagpure and his team adopted the methodology used by the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study, published in The Lancet in October 2020.

Start small, document progress, and scale with the support already waiting for you. Drop a “💪” in comments — I’ll DM a checklist + direct links. #SheStartsHere

caption:
Since its launch in April 2015, the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) has become a transformative force in India’s economic landscape. With over 52+ crore loans worth 33 lakh crore sanctioned across the country, this government-backed initiative continues to uplift micro-entrepreneurs by providing collateral-free financial assistance. From fruit vendors and tailors to salon owners, mechanics, and even startup founders, the scheme has enabled countless small business owners to turn their dreams into thriving enterprises.

The scheme categorizes loans into three segments—Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001–₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh–₹10 lakh)—designed to meet the needs of businesses at various stages of development. What sets PMMY apart is its focus on accessibility and inclusion, especially among women, youth, and marginalized communities in rural and semi-urban areas. By eliminating the need for collateral, it opens doors for first-time entrepreneurs to build self-sustaining ventures.

Recently, the government organized nationwide appreciation events to celebrate success stories of Mudra beneficiaries. These stories highlight how PMMY has been instrumental in fostering self-reliance and grassroots entrepreneurship, aligned with the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat. Entrepreneurs shared heartfelt testimonials, revealing how Mudra loans helped them scale their operations, employ others, and uplift entire communities.

With a decade of impact, the PM Mudra Yojana stands as a beacon of inclusive growth and economic empowerment. Its message rings clear: “PM Mudra Yojana – Fueling Ambitions, Building Futures.”

अगर आप अपना खुद का बिजनेस शुरू करने का सपना देख रहे हैं और पैसों की कमी आड़े आ रही है, तो अब घबराने की जरूरत नहीं है। केंद्र सरकार की प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा योजना (PM Mudra Yojana) के तहत आपको 20 लाख रुपये तक का लोन मिल सकता है। इस योजना का मकसद छोटे व्यापारियों, स्टार्टअप शुरू करने वालों और स्वरोजगार को बढ़ावा देना है। पहले इस योजना में अधिकतम 10 लाख रुपये तक का लोन मिलता था, लेकिन अब तरुण प्लस कैटेगरी जोड़ने के बाद यह सीमा बढ़ाकर 20 लाख रुपये कर दी गई है। मुद्रा योजना के तहत लोन चार कैटेगरी में दिया जाता है – शिशु, किशोर, तरुण और तरुण प्लस। खास बात यह है कि शिशु लोन में किसी भी तरह की गारंटी या गारंटर की जरूरत नहीं होती। इस सरकारी स्कीम के जरिए कोई भी भारतीय नागरिक नॉन-कॉरपोरेट और नॉन-एग्रीकल्चर बिजनेस के लिए लोन ले सकता है। आवेदन की प्रक्रिया बेहद आसान है और आप अपने नजदीकी बैंक या ऑनलाइन माध्यम से भी अप्लाई कर सकते हैं। अगर आपकी उम्र 18 साल से ज्यादा है, बैंक डिफॉल्ट हिस्ट्री नहीं है और आपके पास जरूरी दस्तावेज हैं, तो यह योजना आपके सपनों को हकीकत में बदलने में मदद कर सकती है।

​अक्सर हमें अचानक बिजनेस विस्तार, घर की मरम्मत या किसी इमरजेंसी के लिए फंड्स की जरूरत होती है। ऐसी स्थिति में आपकी पुरानी कार आपके काम आ सकती है!
​मुद्रा कैपिटल (Mudra Capital) की 'कार री-फाइनेंस' सर्विस के साथ आप अपनी वर्तमान कार पर ही लोन प्राप्त कर सकते हैं।
​री-फाइनेंस के फायदे:
✅ पैसे भी और कार भी: आपको अपनी जरूरत के लिए फंड मिल जाता है और कार भी आपके पास ही रहती है।
✅ आसान ईएमआई: पर्सनल लोन के मुकाबले कार लोन की ब्याज दरें अक्सर कम होती हैं।
✅ तेज़ प्रोसेसिंग: कम कागजी कार्यवाही और जल्दी फंड ट्रांसफर।
✅ वर्किंग कैपिटल: छोटे व्यापारियों के लिए बिजनेस में पैसा लगाने का सबसे आसान तरीका।
​आपकी कार की वैल्यू, अब आपके बैंक अकाउंट में! आज ही अपनी कार की वैल्यूएशन कराएं और अपनी वित्तीय जरूरतों को पूरा करें।

caption:
เมืองมรดกโลก | World's Heritage City 
•
Luang Prabang was the capital of the Lan Xang Kingdom during the 13th to 16th centuries. The city is named after Phra Bang (ພະບາງ, Royal Buddha Image in the Dispelling Fear mudra), a statue of Buddha regarded as the most sacred and culturally significant Buddha image in Laos. The Phra Bang arrived in Lan Xang during the reign of Fa Ngum from Angkor and was used to spread Theravada Buddhism in the new kingdom. In 1359, the Khmer king gave the Phra Bang to his son-in-law, the first Lang Xang monarch Fa Ngum (1353–1373), to provide Buddhist legitimacy both to Fa Ngum's rule and by extension to the sovereignty of Laos. The Phra Bang has long been seen by devout Buddhists as a symbol of the right to rule Laos, as only a commendable and virtuous government deserves to be caretaker of such a sacred image. In 1705, it was taken to Vientiane. In 1778, the Siamese invaded Vientiane and captured the Phra Bang, taking it with them to Bangkok. Fast forward to the 21st century, the Phra Bang was moved from the Lao National Museum in Vientiane to the Haw Pha Bang in Luang Prabang. Each year, on the third day of Lao New Year, the statue is taken in procession to Wat Mai. It is exhibited at a shrine, where the Buddha image is ritually bathed by devout laypeople during new year festivities. Luang Prabang was inscribed on the World Heritage list in 1995. Laos had pledged to conserve nature, culture, and history along the confluence of the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers.
•

🚀 Scale Up to ₹20 Lakhs! Are You Using the "Tarun Plus" Mudra Limit? 💸🇮🇳 

Did you know the Mudra Loan limit is now ₹20 lakhs? 

Many entrepreneurs are still planning their growth around the older ₹10 lakh ceiling. However, under the ✨ "Tarun Plus" category, eligible businesses can access double the funding without collateral!

📊 Quick Refresher – Mudra Categories: 

🔹 Shishu: Up to ₹50,000 – For first-time entrepreneurs. 

🔹 Kishore: ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh – For early-stage growth. 

🔹 Tarun: ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh – For expanding operations. 

🔹 🆕 Tarun Plus: ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh – For proven businesses ready to scale. 

💡 Who can apply for Tarun Plus? 

Strict eligibility applies to ensure credit quality: 
 
✅ You must be an existing Tarun borrower. 

✅ You must have successfully repaid your previous Tarun loan. 

✅ You need a clear expansion plan or project report. 

🌟 Why smart entrepreneurs are using it: 
 
✔️ Collateral-free funding (Covered under CGFMU). 

✔️ Ideal for machinery upgrades, larger premises, or entering new markets. 

✔️ Reduces dependence on high-interest private lenders. 

📈 If your business has already shown stability, this is the capital push that takes you from steady → scalable. 

👉 Don’t let lack of awareness limit your growth. If you have a good repayment track record, this facility is waiting for you! 

✍️ CA Syam Sundar Pabbathi

• Gold, Silver and Platinum getting cheaper.
• ⁠1 crore young people will be skilled by India’s top companies in the next five years.
- A 12-month Prime Minister’s Internship will offer a monthly stipend of ₹5,000.

- Salaried employees in the new tax regime stand to save up to ₹17,500 in income tax.
- E-Commerce Export Hubs will be established in PPP mode, enabling MSMEs and traditional artisans to sell their products internationally.

- Andhra Pradesh: ₹15,000 crore allocated for development in the current financial year, with promises of additional funds in the coming years.
- Bihar: ₹26,000 crore allocated for highway development.

Under the proposal being discussed by the Union Finance Ministry and labour bodies, eligible workers will be able to access small unsecured loans without needing property or security as backing, making credit easier and more inclusive for those who normally struggle to obtain bank financing.

The scheme is aimed at improving financial inclusion, boosting self-employment and empowering workers in flexible jobs such as delivery partners, home cleaners, repair technicians and others who lack formal employment benefits.

This initiative is seen as a major step toward fulfilling the social security mandates for gig workers as outlined in the Code on Social Security, providing them with a safety net and formal recognition of their contribution to the digital economy.

#france #french #nagpur #maharashtra

caption:
Mohamed Muizzu, the President of the Maldives, has recently adopted a more conciliatory stance towards India, marking a significant shift from his previous anti-India rhetoric. Despite earlier demands for the repatriation of Indian military personnel and aligning more closely with China, President Muizzu now hails India as the Maldives' "closest ally" and has expressed a desire for debt relief from New Delhi. The Maldives owes India approximately $400.9 million, a substantial debt accumulated over time.

Since his inauguration in November of the previous year, Muizzu's stance towards India has been notably tough, including an immediate demand for the withdrawal of Indian military personnel. These forces, totaling 88 members, were involved in operating three aviation platforms, with a deadline set for their departure by May 10.

In a significant public statement, President Muizzu acknowledged India's role in supporting the Maldives through aid and the implementation of numerous projects. During his first interview with local media since taking office, he emphasized that there should be no doubt about the enduring alliance with India, highlighting the strategic and historical ties binding the two nations.

India's contributions to the Maldives include humanitarian assistance and medical evacuation services, facilitated by two helicopters and a Dornier aircraft. The geographical proximity between the Maldives and India, along with the strategic location in the Indian Ocean Region, underscores the importance of maintaining a positive and cooperative relationship.

President Muizzu has expressed hopes for India's understanding and leniency regarding the Maldives' substantial debt, advocating for a renegotiation of the repayment terms. He has emphasized importance of continuing projects without disruption, indicating potential for positive developments in relations.

This shift in rhetoric comes as the Maldives approaches parliamentary elections in mid-April, suggesting a strategic reevaluation of foreign policy and diplomatic relations by Muizzu's administration.
.

caption:
Reliance Communications, led by Anil Ambani, faced debts of nearly ₹49,000 crore across 53 banks. 

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved a settlement of just ₹455 crore — less than 1% of the original liability — through the insolvency process.

While corporates secure massive loan write-offs, ordinary citizens struggle with personal loans and home loans. 

High interest rates often double individual borrowings, creating a stark contrast between corporate debt restructuring and common borrowers’ financial stress.

This case highlights key issues in India’s banking sector — debt recovery, financial accountability, and economic justice. 

It raises pressing questions about loan write-offs, insolvency laws, and the balance between corporate borrowers and individuals.

caption:
With Saudi Arabia ending loan and oil supply to Pakistan, the decades-long friendship between the two countries has finally ended, reported Middle East Monitor.

This development came after Pakistan Foreign Minister Shah Mehmood Qureshi had given a blunt warning to Saudi Arabia-led Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) for not taking a stance against India over the Kashmir issue.

Qureshi was quoted as saying by the ARY channel, “If you cannot convene it, then I’ll be compelled to ask Prime Minister Imran Khan to call a meeting of the Islamic countries that are ready to stand with us on the issue of Kashmir and support the oppressed Kashmiris.”

The development comes at a time when Pakistan faces a challenging situation as its International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme also remains technically suspended for the last five months.

It is a tough task, given how Saudi Arabia had called in a $ 1 billion loan extended at Imran Khan’s request to bail out the economy in 2018. The Saudi package entailed $3 billion in loans and a $3.2 billion oil credit facility, according to Asian Nikkei Review.

The oil credit facility was suspended in May and the Saudis later asked Pakistan to repay the loan in full. Pakistan repaid the $ 1 billion loan, borrowing from its “iron brother” China.
.
.
.
#TheTatva #TatvaNews #Pakistan #SaudiArabia #UAE #India #Modi #NarendraModi #ImranKhan

caption:
India has pledged over ₹6,300 crore in financial support to the Maldives as part of efforts to address the island nation's foreign exchange crisis, following talks between Maldivian President Mohamed Muizzu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

This financial assistance includes a $400 million currency swap agreement and ₹30 billion under the INR swap window. The two leaders also discussed economic cooperation and maritime security, unveiling a new vision document aimed at bolstering trade, defense, and maritime surveillance in the region.

Modi highlighted India’s ongoing commitment to the Maldives, calling the country India’s “closest neighbour and steadfast friend.” This support marks a turnaround in bilateral ties, which had soured under Muizzu’s administration last year when he campaigned on reducing Maldivian dependence on India and building closer ties with China.

Muizzu acknowledged India’s role in supporting his country during challenging times and emphasized the importance of the new currency swap arrangement to stabilize the Maldivian economy.

The leaders also jointly launched India’s RuPay card in the Maldives to boost tourism and inaugurated a new runway at Hanimaadhoo international airport, constructed with an Indian line of credit worth $132 million. India also handed over 700 housing units built with Indian assistance.

In addition to economic ties, the new vision document aims to enhance the Maldives' maritime security capabilities through Indian radar systems, defense platforms, and patrol vessel refitting.

Modi and Muizzu also discussed cooperation in disaster response, risk mitigation, and combating corruption, alongside signing agreements for police and judicial officer training.

Modi affirmed India’s role as the Maldives' “first responder” in crises and accepted Muizzu’s invitation to visit the Maldives in 2025 to celebrate the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations.

caption:
Launched in April 2015 by the Prime Minister, the Mudra Yojana aims to enable Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), Non-Banking financial institutions/Companies (NBFCs), Small Finance Banks, RBRs, Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, etc. to provide Low Rate Loans to eligible entities. To enable every last mile financer to lend credit to all types of businesses in the country, the MUDRA- Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency bank was established as a public sector financial institution. Low rate loans are provided by micro financers under this scheme. 

ஏப்ரல் 2015 இல் பிரதமரால் தொடங்கப்பட்ட முத்ரா யோஜனா, சிறு நிதி நிறுவனங்கள் (MFIகள்), வங்கி சாரா நிதி நிறுவனங்கள்/நிறுவனங்கள் (NBFCக்கள்), சிறு நிதி வங்கிகள், RBRகள், வணிக வங்கிகள், கூட்டுறவு வங்கிகள் போன்றவற்றுக்கு குறைந்த அளவில் வழங்குவதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது. தகுதியுள்ள நிறுவனங்களுக்கு கடன்களை மதிப்பிடுங்கள். ஒவ்வொரு கடைசி மைல் நிதியளிப்பாளரும் நாட்டில் உள்ள அனைத்து வகையான வணிகங்களுக்கும் கடன் வழங்குவதற்கு, முத்ரா- மைக்ரோ யூனிட்ஸ் டெவலப்மென்ட் மற்றும் மறுநிதியளிப்பு ஏஜென்சி வங்கி ஒரு பொதுத்துறை நிதி நிறுவனமாக நிறுவப்பட்டது. இத்திட்டத்தின் கீழ் மைக்ரோ ஃபைனான்ஸர்களால் குறைந்த விகிதத்தில் கடன் வழங்கப்படுகிறது.

caption:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on September 17 launched the 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme on the occasion of 'Vishwakarma Jayanti', under which traditional craftsmen and artisans will be provided loan assistance at a minimal interest rate without the need for collateral. With a financial outlay of ₹ 13,000 crore for a period of five years, the scheme will benefit about 30 lakh families of traditional artisans and craftsmen, including weavers, goldsmiths, blacksmiths, laundry workers, and barbers. The goal of the scheme is to enhance the accessibility and quality of products and services offered by traditional artisans and craftsmen. The scheme offers collateral-free enterprise development loans of ₹ 1 lakh (first tranche for 18 months repayment) and ₹ 2 lakh (second tranche for 30 months repayment). A concessional rate of interest of 5 percent will be charged from the beneficiary with interest subvention cap of 8 per cent to be paid by the Ministry of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises. The credit guarantee fees will be borne by the central government. Besides, a ₹ 15,000 grant will be provided as a toolkit incentive and an incentive for digital transactions of ₹ 1 per transaction for up to 100 transactions monthly. An artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools and engaged in one of the 18 family-based traditional trades mentioned in the scheme, in the unorganized sector on a self-employment basis, shall be eligible for registration under PM Vishwakarma. The minimum age of the beneficiary should be 18 years on the date of registration.

caption:
प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री भूपेश बघेल ने विधानसभा में कहा- शिक्षित बेरोजगारों को बेरोजगारी भत्ता देने की नई योजना शुरू की जाएगी। रोजगार एवं पंजीयन केन्द्र में रजिस्टर्ड कक्षा 12वीं पास 18 से 35 वर्ष के युवा, जिनके परिवार की वार्षिक आय 2 लाख 50 हजार से कम होगी, उन्हें अधिकतम 2 वर्ष तक 2500 रुपए प्रति माह की दर से बेरोजगारी भत्ता प्रदान करने की घोषणा करता हूं। इसके लिए 2 सौ 50 करोड़ का नई मद में प्रावधान रखा गया है।

मुख्यमंत्री की इन बातों से प्रदेश के बेरोजगारों की उम्मीदें बढ़ी हैं। लाखों युवाओं में खुशी भी है कि उन्हें हर महीने 2500 रुपए की मदद सरकार से बेरोजगारी भत्ते के रूप में मिलेगी। ये भत्ता कब से मिलेगा, कैसे मिलेगा, क्या नियम होंगे, किसे नहीं मिलेगा ये सब कुछ पढ़िए slide कर रिपोर्ट में।

caption:
PM Narendra Modi launches Pradhan Mantri Har Ghar Protein Yojna (PMHP). Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the implementing agency of Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) added new products in their basket such as Dapagliflozin 10mg & Metformin Hydrochloride(Extended Release) 1000mg Tablets  for Diabetes, Jan Aushadhi Protein (High Protein) Powder, Jan Aushadhi Protein for Women (Whey Protein Powder), etc.

Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), which implements Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) regularly analyses various trends of the market and based on the analysis, includes medicines and other products to sell through these Kendras at affordable prices. In the same line, PMBI has now included some new variants of medicines for diabetes and different types of nutraceuticals at affordable prices.

The Government has decided to open 10,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras by 31st December 2023 in the country. A total 9512 Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been opened across the country till 30th June 2023. The product basket of Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) has 1800 medicines, 285 Surgical Equipment and Consumables. These products are available at 50% - 90% lower prices compared to the market.

Keeping in mind the surging issue of diabetes and women health, Jan Aushadhi has decided to make an addition to its already existing list by launching the below-mentioned products in its list and these products are already available in select Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country for common people.

In last 9 years, the number of Kendras have increased by 100 times and the sales have increased more than 170 times. In order to fulfil the achievement of establishing 10,000 Kendras by 31st December 2023, Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) has invited applications from 651 different districts of the country for opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras

BSNL के इस 999 रुपये वाले प्लान में ग्राहकों को मिलने वाले फायदे की बात करें तो इसमें कंपनी प्राइमरी यूजर्स के साथ साथ अन्य कनेक्शन्स वाले ग्राहकों को भी अनलिमिटेड फ्री कॉलिंग ऑफर कर रही है। इसके साथ ही सभी यूजर्स 75GB डेटा मिलने वाला है। मतलब प्लान में कुल 300GB डेटा मिलेगा। इसके अतिरिक्त कंपनी सभी यूजर्स को डेली 100 फ्री एसएमएस भी ऑफर करती है।

caption:
The India AI Impact Summit 2026 began February 16 in New Delhi, bringing together some of the most prominent names in global technology for what is being described as the first major global artificial intelligence summit hosted in the Global South.

The five-day summit is being held across multiple venues in the national capital, including Bharat Mandapam and Sushma Swaraj Bhawan.

It is organised around three pillars — People, Planet and Progress.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Google DeepMind co-founder and CEO Demis Hassabis are among the global technology leaders that will attend the summit.

Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation, is also slated to participate, along with several industry executives and policymakers.

According to organisers, more than 40 CEO and 20 heads of state are expected at the summit, with investment commitments of up to $100 billion under discussion.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to meet 35 to 40 CEOs on the sidelines and will address the main plenary session on February 19.

caption:
PM Modi addresses the 'Grih Pravesham' event in MP

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has addressed the ‘Grih Pravesham’ event in Madhya Pradesh through video conferencing.
Under the ‘Grih Pravesh’ programme, the Prime Minister virtually inaugurated 1.75 lakh houses built under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Rural) in Madhya Pradesh and spoke to the beneficiaries of the scheme from Dhar, Singrauli and Gwalior.
About Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana- Grameen (PMAY-G):
•	Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin (PMAYG) is a scheme for rural housing by the Indian Government. This social welfare program was initiated to meet the objectives of the “Housing for All” scheme by the year 2022.

•	The main aim of the PMAY-G scheme is to provide the pucca house with some of the basic amenities. This scheme is meant for people who do not own a house and people who live in kutcha houses or houses which are severely damaged.

#pm #modi #pmmodi #currentnews #pmmodi🙏👏

ਅਸੀ ਮੌਤ / ਆਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਇੱਕ ਚੁਣਨੀ, ਤੇ ਬੰਨ ਕਾਫਲੇ ਆਵਾਂਗੇ, ਜਿੱਥੋਂ ਮਿਲਣੀ ਜਿੱਤ ਅੰਮੀਏ ਨੀ ਅਸੀਂ ਉੱਥੋਂ ਤੱਕ ਜਾਵਾਂਗੇ...
ਹੁਣ ਉੱਠ ਕੇ ਤੁਰਨਾਂ ਤੇਜ਼ ਪਉ ਗੋਡਿਆਂ ਤੇ ਰੁੜਨਾ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਿਲ ਹੈ, ਅਸੀਂ ਐਸੇ ਰਸਤੇ ਤੁਰ ਪਏ ਹਾਂ ਜਿੱਤੇ ਬਿਨ ਮੁੜਨਾਂ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਿਲ ਹੈ...
ਨੱਥ ਪਾਉਣੀ ਤਾਨਾਸ਼ਾਹੀ ਨੂੰ ਤੇ ਪੁਲਿਸ ਦੀ ਗੁੰਡਾਗਰਦੀ ਨੂੰ, ਆਹ ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਲਕਾਰਗੇਂ ਅਸੀ ਜੁਲਮ ਕਰੇਦੀ ਵਰਦੀ ਨੂੰ, ਹੁਣ ਮਿਲ ਗਏ ਮਕਸਦ ਅੱਗੇ ਦੇ ਤੇ ਵਾਪਸ ਝੁਰਨਾ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਲ ਹੈ, ਅਸੀਂ ਐਸੇ ਰਸਤੇ ਤੁਰ ਪਏ ਹਾਂ ਜਿੱਤੇ ਬਿਨ ਮੁੜਨਾਂ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਿਲ ਹੈ... 
ਅਸੀ ਭਗਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੇ ਸਾਥੀ ਹਾਂ ਤੇ ਪੁੱਤਰ ਬੂਜੇ ਬਾਪੂ ਦੇ, ਸਾਡਾ ਵੈਰ ਲੋਟੂ ਸਰਕਾਰਾਂ ਨੇ ਅਸੀਂ ਵੈਰੀ ਜਗੀਰੂ ਦਾਬੇ ਦੇ, ਵੈਰੀ ਲਈ ਲੋਹਾ ਬਣ ਜਾ ਗੇ ਵਾਂਗੂ ਬਰਫਾਂ ਖੁਰਨਾ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਲ ਹੈ..... ਅਸੀਂ ਐਸੇ ਰਸਤੇ ਤੁਰ ਪਏ ਹਾਂ ਜਿੱਤੇ ਬਿਨ ਮੁੜਨਾਂ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਿਲ ਹੈ...
ਅਸੀ ਵਾਂਗੂੰ ਸੰਤ ਸਿਪਾਹੀ ਦੇ ਬਾਪੂ ਜਾਨ ਤਲੀ ਤੇ ਰੱਖਾਗੇ, ਕਰ ਚੇਤੇ ਬੰਦੇ ਬਹਾਦਰ ਨੂੰ ਪਈ ਲੋੜ ਤਾਂ ਸ਼ਸ਼ਤਰ ਚੱਕਾਗੇਂ, ਬਈ ਇਤਹਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਜਾਣੇ ਪਹਿਚਾਣੇ ਦੀ ਅੱਗੇ ਵੱਲ ਤੁਰਨਾ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਲ ਹੈ.. ਅਸੀਂ ਐਸੇ ਰਸਤੇ ਤੁਰ ਪਏ ਹਾਂ ਜਿੱਤੇ ਬਿਨ ਮੁੜਨਾਂ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਿਲ ਹੈ... #farmersprotest #farmer #farmersmarket #modikissanvirodhi

Today’s Rescue #Story is filled with sloppy kisses & warm hugs. Meet Iteeshree Modi from #Gujarat,  India🇮🇳. She’s here to share tidbits of her wonderful life:
“My #pet Babboo is 6 and half years now and is a rescue baby. I found him abandoned on the road.
